item.title: [7] Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
item.description:
Last authors: Jiangping Hu, Chen Fang

Authors: Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, Rui-Heng Liu, Jiangping Hu, Chen Fang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical work on Fractional Chern Insulators and Hubbard interactions, relevant to FQHE and strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #theory #fractionalquantumHall #stronglycorrelated #Cherninsulator

Abstract: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

item.title: [8] Umklapp-enhanced high-Tc topological superconductivity mediated by magnons in p-wave magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Kristoffer Leraand, Asle Sudb{\o}

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory proposing magnon-mediated topological superconductivity in p-wave magnets with Majorana flat bands.

Tags: #theory #topologicalsuperconductor #superconductivity #magnons #Majorana

Abstract: We show that magnon exchange can induce nodal topological superconductivity in a microscopic model of a $p$-wave magnet. Solving the weak-coupling multiband gap equation for itinerant electrons exchange-coupled to localized spins, we find a nodal $p$-wave gap and a critical temperature that rises sharply as the Fermi surface approaches the magnetic Brillouin-zone boundary. In this regime, small-reduced-momentum magnons can scatter electrons between Fermi-surface segments on opposite sides of the zone. These Umklapp processes enhance pairing because the contributions from different sites in the magnetic unit cell cancel less in their electron-magnon vertices than in those for ordinary scattering at comparable reduced momenta. Momentum-resolved winding numbers predict zero-energy Majorana flat bands at symmetry-preserving edges where the bulk nodes project to distinct momenta.

item.title: [7] First order vortex-unbinding transition in 2D topological superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Vera Mikheeva, Elio J. K\"onig

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of vortex physics and Majorana modes in 2D topological superconductors with experimental signatures.

Tags: #theory #topologicalsuperconductor #Majorana #vortices

Abstract: We study the fate of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition in a two-dimensional topological superconductor whose vortex cores each host an isolated Majorana zero mode, energetically well separated from the bulk gap and other bound states of the vortex. When the Majorana localization length $\xi_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $\xi$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We construct an effective field theory for the resulting dilute vortex gas, coupling the ordinary BKT phase field to an additional field encoding the Majorana-mediated interaction, and show, using renormalization-group and instanton methods, that this hybridization can drive the transition first order, with the metastable phase decaying at an exponentially small rate. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

item.title: [7] Anyon Coherent States in Fractional Chern Insulators
item.description:
Last authors: Haylen Gerhard, Wladimir A. Benalcazar

Authors: Pedro Fittipaldi de Castro, Haylen Gerhard, Wladimir A. Benalcazar

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of anyon coherent states in Fractional Chern Insulators and FQH systems.

Tags: #theory #fractionalquantumHall #Cherninsulator #anyons

Abstract: In fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, coherent anyonic excitations are the natural entities for describing anyon dynamics, their interactions, and braiding, yet no general expression for their wavefunctions is known beyond Laughlin's quasiholes. We introduce a systematic, operator-based construction of maximally-localized wavefunctions of anyons of either charge in FQH states and fractional Chern insulators, including those in non-ideal, non-vortexable bands. We find that these wavefunctions describe coherent quasiparticles: zero modes of local annihilation operators that saturate projected-density uncertainty bounds. These coherent states owe their existence to a nontrivial topology of the anyon band, with the winding of their Bloch coefficients encoding an anyon band's Chern number. As such, their guiding centers exist anywhere within the lattice, and their mutual overlaps decay as Gaussians determined by the effective magnetic length of the anyon band.

item.title: [7] Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
item.description:
Last authors: Roni Ilan, Raquel Queiroz

Authors: Carolina Paiva, Bruno Mera, Roni Ilan, Raquel Queiroz

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for topological equivalence using wave-function overlaps, relevant to Chern and Z2 invariants.

Tags: #theory #topology #Chernnumber #Z2invariant #bandstructure

Abstract: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

item.title: [8] Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
item.description:
Last authors: L\'aszl\'o Szunyogh, Ulrich Nowak

Authors: Tobias Dannegger, Julian A. Beisch, Levente R\'ozsa, L\'aszl\'o Szunyogh, Ulrich Nowak

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ab initio study of altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite, a direct user interest.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #magnetism #spintronics #electronic_structure

Abstract: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the {\Gamma} point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

item.title: [7] Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb -Na2PrO3 revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
item.description:
Last authors: Yurii Skourski, Radu Coldea

Authors: Kylie MacFarquharson, Ryutaro Okuma, Matthew Pearce, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop in a honeycomb magnet.

Tags: #magnetism #experiment #honeycomb_lattice #antiferromagnetism

Abstract: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $\alpha$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

item.title: [7] Circuit model for gate-induced excitation of quantum Hall edges tuned by DC gate bias
item.description:
Last authors: Takaaki Mano, Go Yusa

Authors: Kodai Sugizaki, Takaaki Mano, Go Yusa

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of gate-induced excitations at quantum Hall edges, a broader user interest.

Tags: #quantum_Hall #experiment #transport #mesoscopic_physics

Abstract: Edge excitations, which propagate along the edge of a quantum Hall system, are of great interest in the study of low-dimensional electron systems and mesoscopic transport phenomena. In this study, we investigate the relationship between the input voltage and the excitation waveform for gate-induced excitations. By varying the offset voltage applied to the gate, we observe that the excitation waveform changes from a first-derivative-like response to a response proportional to the input waveform in the time domain. In the frequency domain, we observe that the frequency dependence of the gate excitation changes significantly as the offset voltage crosses the pinch-off voltage. We show that these changes can be described by a single equivalent circuit model with different effective gate-2DEG capacitances on either side of the pinch-off voltage. In addition, we confirm that the effective capacitance obtained from the fitting of the model with the experimental data is consistent with the capacitance calculated from the device structure.

item.title: [8] Magnetic order in Tb and Dy substituted La3Ni2O7 and effects of high-pressure high-temperature O2 annealing
item.description:
Last authors: Jeffrey W. Lynn, M. Brian Maple

Authors: Yuhang Deng, Farhad Taraporevala, Jui-Chia Lee, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnetic order and superconductivity in substituted nickelate La3Ni2O7, a user interest.

Tags: #superconductivity #nickelates #magnetism #experiment #density_wave

Abstract: To study the influence of magnetic lanthanide (Ln) substituents on La3Ni2O7, polycrystalline samples of La3-xLnxNi2O7 (Ln = Pr, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, and Yb) were synthesized and characterized by electrical transport, magnetization, and x-ray and neutron powder diffraction before and after high-pressure high-temperature oxygen annealing. The annealing process led to the formation of La3Ni2O7 polymorphs and more metallic-like temperature dependence of the electrical resistance while changing the density-wave transition temperature only slightly. For unannealed La2.7Tb0.3Ni2O7 and La2.7Dy0.3Ni2O7, distinct features in the magnetic susceptibility and additional magnetic peaks in neutron diffraction patterns indicate that both samples develop long-range magnetic order below ~13 and 11 K, respectively. The magnetic signatures were strongly suppressed following oxygen annealing, suggesting a possible association with the accompanying structural modifications. These behaviors distinguish Tb and Dy from Pr, Nd, and Sm substituents which do not introduce magnetic ordering in the system, establishing La3-xTbxNi2O7 and La3-xDyxNi2O7 as promising platforms for exploring the interplay between magnetic order and pressure-induced superconductivity in La3Ni2O7.

item.title: [7] Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
item.description:
Last authors: H. -K. Mao, V. V. Struzhkin

Authors: A. G. Gavriliuk, I. A. Troyan, A. A. Mironovich, A. G. Ivanova, H. -K. Mao, V. V. Struzhkin

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of local field screening and critical state in high-pressure superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #experiment #high_pressure #magnetism

Abstract: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe M\"ossbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

item.title: [8] Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
item.description:
Last authors: Julie Karel, Nikhil V. Medhekar

Authors: Thanh Tung Huynh, Yuefeng Yin, Weiyao Zhao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: First-principles study of spin Hall conductivity from Berry curvature in halide perovskites, a direct interest.

Tags: #theory #Berry_curvature #spin_Hall_effect #electronic_structure #spintronics

Abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric double-layer gating CsPbI3 attains the spin Hall conductivity of p-GaAs. The response is therefore determined by the position of the halide-p bands relative to the valence band maximum, not by the atomic spin-orbit constant, a criterion that applies to any semiconductor with an orbital-singlet band edge. These results point to CsPbI3 as a candidate gate-controlled source of spin current for perovskite spin-orbit torque devices.

item.title: [7] Topological Bound States in the Continuum
item.description:
Last authors: J. Villavicencio, Pierre A. Pantaleon

Authors: Dan-Na Liu, J. Villavicencio, Pierre A. Pantaleon

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of topological bound states and valley topology in bilayer graphene.

Tags: #theory #graphene #topological #bilayer

Abstract: We uncover topological bound states in the continuum in AB-stacked bilayer graphene mass-wall junctions. Valley topology supports interface states propagating along the wall, while a distinct winding of the confinement conditions governs exact decoupling from conducting leads. Tuning the junction length or interlayer bias can merge oppositely charged bound states and remove confinement without changing the valley topology. At generic critical points, the state remains bound and nearby resonance widths open quartically with momentum. These results connect complementary roles of topology in interface propagation and confinement within a conducting continuum.

item.title: [9] Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands
item.description:
Last authors: Cheng Huang, Zi Yang Meng

Authors: Shibo Shan, Cheng Huang, Zi Yang Meng

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: QMC study of interaction effects and flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene, a core user interest.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #theory #twisted_bilayer_graphene #strongly_correlated_electrons #flat_bands #electronic_structure #Mott

Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts strong correlation effects within topological flat bands separated from remote dispersive bands. This separation motivates projection onto the central bands, which greatly reduces the computational complexity of many-body calculations, including momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. However, the interaction-induced Mott gap obtained in the projected model can be comparable to the noninteracting flat--remote band separation, raising the question of whether the projection remains valid. Here, we extend momentum-space QMC to explicitly include remote BM bands within a broad energy window at charge neutrality. We find that the projected description remains reliable over a broad parameter regime, up to $u_0/u_1\lesssim0.9$: the projected and remote-band calculations yield similar low-energy electron and trion spectra, and the Kramers intervalley-coherent ground state remains stable. In particular, the Dirac trion remains robust in the finite-temperature normal state when remote bands are included. Near the band-touching limit $u_0=u_1$, remote-band electrons acquire substantial low-energy spectral weight, accompanied by suppression of the trion weight and loss of the Kramers intervalley-coherent state. Our findings establish the broad validity of flat-band projection while reconciling the projected and THF viewpoints by identifying the near-band-touching regime in which explicit remote-band degrees of freedom become essential.

item.title: [9] Scattering Circular Dichroism from Spatially Modulated Anisotropic Magnetic Dipoles in BiFeO3
item.description:
Last authors: T. Arima, Y. Yamasaki

Authors: Y. Ishii, N. Sasabe, T. Honda, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Experimental study of circular dichroism revealing spatially modulated anisotropic magnetic dipoles in multiferroic BiFeO3, connecting to altermagnetism and TRSB.

Tags: #experiment #altermagnetism #time_reversal_symmetry_breaking #circular_dichroism #multiferroics #magnetism

Abstract: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

item.title: [7] Thermally driven multiple sliding states and avalanche dynamics in rhombohedral Pb(TaSe2)2 nanoflakes (Materials Today)
item.description:
Last authors: Ruiya Zhan, Xiao Lin

Authors: Zhuokai Xu, Xiaohui Yang, Zhefeng Lou, et al.

Published as: Materials Today DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of sliding dynamics and resistive switching in van der Waals nanoflakes.

Tags: #vanderWaals #transport #experiment #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Interlayer sliding in van der Waals materials offers a promising route to control functional properties, yet a comprehensive understanding of the complex collective domain dynamics governing these transitions remains challenging. Here, we investigate thermally driven sliding dynamics in Pb(TaSe2)2 nanoflakes, incorporating transport and atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) measurements. Reducing the flake thickness induces multiple stepwise resistance jumps with enhanced hysteresis, corresponding to transitions between stacking domains accompanied by ripplocations. Statistical analysis of the jumps reveals collective avalanche behavior of domain dynamics with universal power-law scaling, quantifying the domain motion. Harnessing these features, we demonstrate controllable, non-volatile multi-level resistive switching, including write/erase operations, via thermal cycling. These findings provide valuable insights into the sliding dynamics for various 2D materials, with significant implications for the development of slidetronics devices.

item.title: [8] Field-free deterministic spin-orbit torque magnetization switching using monolayer WTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Saroj P Dash, Bhaskaran Muralidharan

Authors: Ganesh Hanchanahal, Arnav Jain, Shrushti Tapar, Saroj P Dash, Bhaskaran Muralidharan

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental and modeling study of spin-orbit torque in monolayer WTe2, a relevant 2D topological material.

Tags: #spintronics #monolayer #WTe2 #topologicalmaterials #magnetism

Abstract: An important step towards the practical implementation of spin-orbit torque magnetic memory is the field-free switching of the magnetization vector. In this work, we investigate spin-orbit torque-driven magnetization dynamics and switching devices comprising monolayer $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ as the spin-source material. We perform a comparative analysis of the two phases of $\mathrm{WTe}_2$, namely the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ and $1\mathrm{T}'$ with the necessary symmetries for field-free deterministic magnetization switching. We demonstrate switching in both systems and analyse the dependence of the switching dynamics on the applied bias voltage, ribbon orientation and width of the magnetic layer. Modelling the ferromagnet as an exchange-coupled macrospin within a non-equilibrium Green's function framework, we find that the $x$-ribbon geometry of the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ phase generates a significantly larger current-induced spin polarization than the $1\mathrm{T}'$ phase, resulting in a larger damping-like torque on the adjacent magnetic layer and faster switching. The switching time of $1\mathrm{T}'$ devices varies strongly and non-monotonically with the width of the magnetic layer. In $1\mathrm{T}_d$ devices, it remains nearly constant over a broad range of widths, consistent with an edge-dominated torque. These results identify $x$-ribbon $1\mathrm{T}_d$-$\mathrm{WTe}_2$ as a promising spin source for field-free SOT-MRAM.

item.title: [9] Current-driven resistive switching in high-field heavy fermion metal UTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Priscila F. S. Rosa, Philip J. W. Moll

Authors: Ling Zhang (Mark), Chunyu (Mark), Guo, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental study on current-driven phase transitions in the heavy fermion superconductor UTe2.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #heavyfermion #superconductivity #UTe2 #transport #correlatedelectrons

Abstract: In UTe$_2$, superconductivity persists up to 70 T for fields tilted by roughly 20-40{\deg} from the b axis toward c. Its normal state is a field-polarized (FP) state, which emerges above a first-order metamagnetic transition when the field component along b exceeds $\sim$35 T. Despite being the parent of this high-field superconductivity, the FP state remains poorly understood, including whether it shares underlying physics with the low-field paramagnetic (PM) state from which it is abruptly separated. Using microstructures fabricated by focused ion beam, we reach current densities of 30-60 kA/cm2 and observe a current-induced high-resistivity state in both the PM and FP regimes over a wide range of field angles in the bc plane. Above a critical current density of order 10 kA/cm2, the resistivity sharply rises to values comparable to those near the critical end point of the metamagnetic transition. The critical current density increases with temperature, opposite to the trend expected from Joule heating, ruling out a thermal origin. The emergence of the same instability on both sides of the metamagnetic transition reveals an unexpected commonality between the FP and PM states. More broadly, the observation of a current-induced transition in a heavy-fermion metal exposes the multitude of nearby electronic states in correlated electron systems and shows that electric current, like magnetic field and pressure, can switch between them.

item.title: [8] Helices at Twisted Ferroelectric Interfaces
item.description:
Last authors: Tchavdar Todorov, J. Marty Gregg

Authors: Kristina Holsgrove, Ronan Lynch, Conor McCluskey, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of helices and chirality at twisted ferroelectric oxide interfaces, relevant to twistronics.

Tags: #twistedinterfaces #ferroelectrics #oxidematerials #4DSTEM #topology

Abstract: We report that twisted interfaces, formed between two ferroelectric lithium niobate single crystals, contain arrays of coherently bonded and elastically deformed nanoscale structural helices, separated from one another by screw dislocations. The helices generate remarkable contrast in four dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) and through related differential phase contrast (DPC). Such images have been successfully rationalised by modelling the trajectory of electrons that channel along helical pathways as they traverse the interface, but the structural helices implied have also been directly imaged using electron ptychography. Importantly, as lithium niobate is a uniaxial ferroelectric, the torsional strain in these structural helices necessarily also causes dipolar helices to form, inferred through consideration of pertinent piezoelectric tensors and flexoelectric coefficients. Helices are topologically distinct from the more commonly reported vortices and, importantly, they are chiral. Helical (and hence chiral) character was confirmed by observing that DPC images were identical before and after the sample was inverted. Chirality was also established through second harmonic optical circularly-polarised dichroism measurements, in which unusually large interfacial signals were seen. It must be stressed that the arrays of helices observed are distinct from moir\'e patterns; they facilitate lattice rotation combining plastic and elastic deformation and are not simply a superposition of lattices, twisted with respect to one another. Thus, intimately bonded twisted oxide interfaces will have distinctly different characteristics from those of twisted stacks of two-dimensional van der Waals materials, opening up a new and distinct kind of twistronics.

item.title: [7] Higher-order magnetic hopfions in uniaxial chiral magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, Nikolai S. Kiselev

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of higher-order magnetic hopfions in chiral magnets, relevant to topological magnetism.

Tags: #theory #topologicalmagnetism #chiralmagnets #magnetictextures

Abstract: Chiral magnets host hopfions, but their experimentally observed configurations are largely limited to hopfion rings, heliknotons, and their clusters. Here, we show that uniaxial anisotropy stabilizes a diverse family of knotted and linked hopfions with zero and arbitrary positive Hopf indices. We identify their stability regions in the anisotropy -- field parameter space and introduce a systematic construction based on mapping skyrmion braids into three-dimensional magnetic textures. We find that the minimum energy of stable hopfions increases approximately linearly with the Hopf index.

item.title: [10] momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
item.description:
Last authors: Stefan Mathias (I. Physikalisches Institut, International Center for Advanced Studies of Energy Conversion)

Authors: Paul Werner (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Software package for time-resolved momentum microscopy (ARPES) data analysis, directly relevant to user's method.

Tags: #ARPES #methodology #dataanalysis #photoemission #bandstructure

Abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

item.title: [9] Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
item.description:
Last authors: Shiyu Deng, Marie-Bernadette Lepetit

Authors: Ramasamy Murugesan, Shiyu Deng, Marie-Bernadette Lepetit

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ab-initio study of magnetic interactions in nickelates, a key correlated electron system, with RIXS connection.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #nickelates #ab-initio #RIXS #correlatedelectrons #magnetism #electronicstructure

Abstract: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.

item.title: [9] Multicharged Kramers-Weyl Fermions, Quantum Geometric Hall Responses and de Haas-van Alphen Oscillations in WAl2
item.description:
Last authors: Meet Shah, Prafulla K. Jha

Authors: Saurav Patel, Meet Shah, Prafulla K. Jha

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: First-principles study of Weyl fermions, Berry curvature, and quantum oscillations in a real material.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #Weylsemimetal #Berrycurvature #topological #DFT #Fermisurface #transport #quantumoscillations

Abstract: Quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions and crystalline symmetries play a central role in condensed matter physics, shaping the electronic topology and physical responses of solids. In particular, Kramers-Weyl fermions, spin-split Fermi surfaces probed through quantum oscillations and quantum geometric nonlinear Hall and intrinsic spin Hall responses have garnered significant attention. Despite progress in understanding these phenomena individually, their coexistence with topological surface states, Fermi arcs and chirality dependent quantum geometric transport remains scarce, as pronounced responses involve suitable symmetries, SOC and Fermi surface geometry. Here, we explore this synergy in experimentally synthesized WAl$_2$, considering both structural enantiomers using first-principles calculations and symmetry analysis. We observed twelve Kramers-Weyl (KW) crossings with quantized chiral charges $|C|=1$ and $|C|=3$, accompanied by nontrivial surface states and Fermi arcs. The pronounced metallic character gives rise to six Fermi surface sheets exhibiting antisymmetric SOC, with distinct extremal orbits and candidate spin-split pairs resolved through calculated de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) quantum oscillations. The electronic structure also exhibits large intrinsic Berry curvature dipole (BCD) arising from the asymmetric distribution of Berry curvature, giving rise to a nonlinear Hall response. The opposite structural handedness of the two enantiomers reverses the chiralities and BCD, reversing the direction of Fermi arcs and nonlinear Hall current. BCD attains $|D_{zz}|\approx0.338$, yielding nonlinear Hall current densities $|j_x|\approx5.04\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $|j_y|\approx2.52\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. We observe enhanced SHC associated with triply charged KW point at $\Gamma$, suggesting role of higher Chern number in the SHC.

item.title: [8] Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Oleg V. Yazyev, Andras Kis

Authors: Asmund Ottesen, Shun Feng, Edoardo Lopriore, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on exciton control and transport in few-layer 2D heterostructures.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #heterostructure #excitons #ferroelectricity #opticalspectroscopy

Abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons. Our optical probe reveals intermediate states of vertically aligned interfacial polarisation with magnitudes that confirm cumulative polarisation in multilayers. Overall, our work presents sliding ferroelectricity as a powerful tool to tune interlayer coupling and layer hybridisation. These results represent a step toward ferroelectric-controlled exciton interconnects and novel multi-bit optical memories.

item.title: [8] Spectral localizers in phase space: Z and Z2 invariants for higher-order, semimetal, and valley modes
item.description:
Last authors: Lucien Jezequel, Christophe Mora

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Unified theoretical framework for topological gapless modes in Dirac semimetals and TIs.

Tags: #theory #topological #Diracsemimetal #topologicalinsulator #bandstructure

Abstract: Topologically protected gapless modes emerge across multiple platforms, ranging from nodes in the band structure to boundary states in topologically non-trivial insulators, with each case governed by distinct topological classifications and invariants. Here, we generalize the spectral localizer method to establish a unified framework for topological gapless modes. The spectral localizer reduces the original Hamiltonian to a zero-dimensional operator by recursively applying quantum confining operators, which need not be diagonal in either position or momentum space, as previously assumed. In phase space, the zero-manifold of the semiclassical confining operators forms a shell enclosing the gapless mode of interest, analogous to the Teo-Kane framework for topological defects. The localizer yields a zero-dimensional invariant, such as a signature, a determinant sign, or a Pfaffian sign, capturing both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ classifications. This single construction thus encompasses diverse scenarios, including hinge modes in higher-order topological insulators, individual Dirac nodes in semimetals, and valley-selective topological boundary modes. We illustrate our approach using lattice models in symmetry classes A, AIII, AII, and D, verifying that topological transitions coincide with a vanishing gap in the spectral localizer operator.

item.title: [8] Quantum Metric Control of Topological Superconductivity and Incommensurate Charge Density Wave in an Interacting Lieb-Kitaev Chain Model
item.description:
Last authors: K. T. Law, Xiao Yan Xu

Authors: Jiale Xuan, Grant Z. X. Yang, K. T. Law, Xiao Yan Xu

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Theoretical model exploring CDW, topological superconductivity, Majorana modes, and quantum metric.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #theoretical #CDW #topologicalsuperconductivity #Majorana #quantummetric

Abstract: We study an interacting spinless Lieb-Kitaev chain model in the nearly flat-band regime, motivated by the recent observation that Majorana zero modes in the noninteracting Lieb-Kitaev system inherit two decay modes: an ordinary Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) length and a longer geometric length controlled by the quantum metric. By tuning both the interaction strength and quantum metric, we identify a topological superconducting (TSC) phase, an incommensurate charge-density-wave (ICDW)phase, and a commensurate charge-density-wave (CDW) phase. Inside the TSC phase, the QML is enhanced when increasing the interactions. In the ICDW phase, the interactions are modulated by quantum metric to generate an effective chemical potential, leading to a discontinuous incommensurate-to-commensurate (IC-C) transition. We verify these phases and conclusions using low energy effective theory and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations.

item.title: [7] Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
item.description:
Last authors: Jiancheng Lv, Kazunari Matsuda

Authors: Zhiwei Li, Yuhao Zhou, Yikai Yang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: AI/ML framework for accelerating DFT electronic structure and band prediction, highly relevant to user.

Tags: #methodology #DFT #electronicstructure #AI/ML

Abstract: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

item.title: [8] Geometric formulation of the orbital magnetic susceptibility of periodic insulators
item.description:
Last authors: J. W. F. Venderbos

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical formulation of orbital magnetic susceptibility, quantum geometry, and Dirac semimetals.

Tags: #theoretical #Diracsemimetal #quantumgeometry #magneticsusceptibility

Abstract: A gauge-invariant projector-based expression for the orbital magnetic susceptibility of periodic insulators is obtained from a density-matrix perturbation expansion in a uniform magnetic field. It is shown that, within such an approach, it is natural to distinguish two contributions: the Van Vleck paramagnetic contribution and a geometric contribution. The latter can be expressed in terms of fundamental geometric quantities built from projector derivatives such as the curvature and metric operators, as well as the closely related magnetic moment operator. When applied to two-band and four-band models, the expression for the susceptibility reduces to a simplified formula expressed in terms of the quantum metric. The significance of quantum geometry for the orbital magnetic response is then examined within a lattice model in two dimensions describing the transition between two distinct insulators via a Dirac semimetallic phase.

item.title: [7] Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
item.description:
Last authors: Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann

Authors: Paul Herrgen, Stephan Wust, Christin Schmitt, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of ultrafast demagnetization in antiferromagnets, relevant to magnetic materials.

Tags: #experimental #antiferromagnetism #ultrafastdynamics

Abstract: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

item.title: [8] Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
item.description:
Last authors: Federico Garcia-Gaitan, Branislav K. Nikolic

Authors: Jalil Varela-Manjarres, Federico Garcia-Gaitan, Branislav K. Nikolic

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Explains magnon dynamics in 2D antiferromagnetic CrSBr, relevant for magnetic quantum materials.

Tags: #magnon #exciton #phonon #antiferromagnet #2Dmaterials #spintronics

Abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

Why: Theory on local orbital magnetization and Chern markers for inhomogeneous magnetic/topological materials, direct relevance.

Tags: #theory #loopcurrent #Chern #topological #magnetism

Abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global St\v{r}eda relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

item.title: [7] Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
item.description:
Last authors: Vladimir Juri\v{c}i\'c, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on fractional charge at dislocations in topological crystals, relevant for Weyl semimetals.

Tags: #theory #topological #Weylsemimetal #crystaldefects

Abstract: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

item.title: [8] Strange metal at the Lifshitz transition (Sci. China-Phys. Mech. Astron.)
item.description:
Last authors: Wu-Ming Liu, Xiao-Tian Zhang

Authors: Yi-Hui Xing, Wu-Ming Liu, Xiao-Tian Zhang

Published as: Sci. China-Phys. Mech. Astron. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on strange metal behavior in relevant materials (cuprates, graphene, twisted bilayer) with electronic structure implications.

Tags: #theory #stronglycorrelated #graphene #twistedbilayer #cuprates #electronicstructure #transport #STS

Abstract: Strange metal behavior is widely observed in cuprates, ruthenates, and twisted bilayer graphene. We study quantum critical transport at a two-dimensional Lifshitz transition, where the Fermi surface hosts a van Hove singularity and changes from convex to concave. Self-consistently solving the fermion-boson coupled system, we demonstrate a linear-in-$1/\omega$ optical conductivity driven by the interplay between impurity and critical scattering. The resistivity exhibits a persistent linear-in-$T$ in the quantum critical regime down to $T\rightarrow 0$. Spatially fluctuating Yukawa interaction further extends the linear-in-$T$ regime, providing a unified mechanism for strange metallic transport at the Lifshitz transition.

item.title: [9] Altermagnets versus Antiferromagnets
item.description:
Last authors: V. P. Mineev

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on altermagnets, Berry curvature, and anomalous Hall, directly matching multiple strong user interests.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #Berrycurvature #anomalousHall #electronicstructure #magneticmaterials

Abstract: Altermagnets are substances with a momentum-dependent spin splitting of electron bands due to a specific crystal structure that is invariant under time reversal only in combination with rotations and reflections. The developed phenomenological approach allows to obtain a spectrum of electron bands in altermagnets corresponding to their magnetic group symmetry. We consider antiferromagnetic, weak ferromagnetic, and ferrimagnetic structures. The calculated Berry curvature of electron bands in the altermagnet with zero spontaneous magnetisation occurs an odd function of momentum components whereas it is even in a weak ferromagnetic state. The Berry curvature in ferrimagnetic state consists of sum of even and odd terms.

item.title: [9] Magnetic field control of the excitonic transition in Ta2NiSe5 (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Giacomo Mazza

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on magnetic field control in a related material, featuring excitonic insulator and user-specific loop currents.

Tags: #theory #excitonicinsulator #magneticfield #loopcurrent #phonons #Ta2NiSe5

Abstract: The formation of excitonic insulator phases in quantum materials is often masked by structural distortions caused by the coupling between electronic and phononic order parameters. Here, for the candidate material Ta$_2$NiSe$_5$, we show that sufficiently high magnetic fields can stabilize an excitonic insulating phase in the absence of a lattice distortion. By considering the interplay between the excitonic and structural instabilities, we predict a magnetic field-induced transition from the low-temperature, structurally distorted, semiconducting phase to an undistorted excitonic insulator phase with ground-state loop currents. Before the transition, the magnetic field-softening of the phonon mode associated with the structural distortion reveals the existence of a latent excitonic phase under the structurally distorted one. These results highlight an unbiased route towards the disentanglement of the coupled excitonic-structural transition in Ta$_2$NiSe$_5$, and uncover a general mechanism for magnetic field control of competing phases in quantum materials.

item.title: [8] Magneto-optical transport in type-II Weyl semimetals in the presence of orbital magnetic moment (Phys. Scr.)
item.description:
Last authors: Panchlal Prabhat, Amit Gupta

Published as: Phys. Scr. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for magneto-optical transport in type-II Weyl semimetals, with experimental signatures.

Tags: #Weylsemimetal #Berrycurvature #transport #theory

Abstract: In this work, we investigate the linear and nonlinear magnetoconductivity of tilted type-II Weyl semimetals within the semiclassical Boltzmann framework by incorporating both the Berry curvature (BC) and the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) corrections. In the linear response regime, we derive analytical expressions for the magnetoconductivity that explicitly include the previously ignored OMM contribution while in the nonlinear regime we obtain analytical expressions that account for the combined effects of the BC and OMM. We find that the open Fermi surface and finite density of states characteristic of the type-II phase qualitatively alter the BC and OMM-induced transport responses relative to the type-I case. Depending on the magnetic-field orientation and transport geometry, the OMM is shown to either suppress or enhance different magnetoconductivity components, in contrast to their monotonic behavior in type-I Weyl semimetals. Our results provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for magneto-optical transport in tilted type-II Weyl semimetals and identify experimentally accessible signatures of the interplay between cone tilt, BC and OMM in candidate materials such as WTe$_2$, MoTe$_2$ and TaIrTe$_4$.

item.title: [8] Unconventional magnetic field response of X-ray magnetic circular dichroism in -Fe2O3
item.description:
Last authors: N. Sasabe, Y. Yamasaki

Authors: Y. Ishii, N. Sasabe, Y. Yamasaki

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of altermagnetism in hematite using XMCD, a relevant topic and technique.

Tags: #altermagnetism #XMCD #experimental #magneticmaterial

Abstract: Altermagnets are compensated collinear magnets that break time-reversal symmetry without net magnetization, enabling unconventional magneto-optical responses. Here, we experimentally demonstrate X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) in hematite $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ for X-rays incident along the [111] direction, perpendicular to the applied magnetic field and the weak ferromagnetic moment induced by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The XMCD amplitude reaches approximately 10 \% of the polarization-averaged X-ray absorption intensity, whereas it is nearly suppressed for $\mathbf{H}\parallel[1\bar{1}0]$ of 200 mT. This unique behavior is consistent with field-driven changes between configurations associated with different magnetic symmetries. Our results establish that XMCD in the altermagnet $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ exhibits a fundamentally distinct response compared to that of weak ferromagnetism. This study addresses how XMCD in altermagnets responds to external magnetic fields compared to conventional ferromagnets.

item.title: [7] Disorder-free many-body localization in real quantum materials
item.description:
Last authors: Dao Xiang, Jiaqing He

Authors: Yingpeng Qi, Jianmin Yang, Zhihui Zhou, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental identification of disorder-free many-body localization in a real material (AgCrSe2).

Tags: #many-bodylocalization #correlated #flatband #topological #experimental #quantummaterials

Abstract: Quantum many-body interactions and strong correlation effects facilitate the emergence of new quantum states and exotic properties in condensed matter systems. One of outstanding questions in this field is whether a non-ergodic and non-thermalizing state solely driven by strong correlations, i.e. the disorder-free many-body localization (DFMBL) phase, exist in condensed matter systems. In this work, using a novel Bragg scattering phase breaking approach and sophisticated theoretical simulation, we unambiguously identify this two-dimensional quantum state in the real material system of AgCrSe2. The strong correlations among in-plane Ag atoms give rise to significant phononic flat bands and static two-dimensional off-center displacements of Ag atoms ranging from 0 to 0.5 angstrom with non-ergodic behavior. With a few representative materials, we prove that low-energy phononic flat bands serve as a promising indicator for a catalogue of DFMBL materials. As temperature rising, this static localization state with multiple degenerate local configurations persists up to near room temperature before transforming into a dynamically correlated state at a higher temperature. Emergent vibrational modes in the THz range and star-like topological structures constitute the low-energy excitation in the DFMBL phase. Moreover, the atomic engineering of a single Ag atom position induces a collective, correlated triangular motif, manifesting a generalized Winger solid in the atomic degree of freedom and underpinning the DFMBL regime. The identified DFMBL phase in a real material system offers a unified framework for understanding the rich quantum phenomena, such as the boson peak, the Debye-Einstein two-channel thermal conductivity and the spiral spin liquid state in quantum materials, and also offers a promising platform for topologically protected quantum computation and quantum memory.

item.title: [7] Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases in the Triangular Majorana-Hubbard Ladder
item.description:
Last authors: Jian-Xin Zhu, Armin Rahmani

Authors: Will Holdhusen, Alberto Nocera, Jian-Xin Zhu, Armin Rahmani

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Theoretical study of symmetry-protected topological phases with interacting Majorana modes, with material context.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #Majorana #topologicalsuperconductor #Hubbardmodel #theory

Abstract: We uncover a family of symmetry-protected topological phases in a model of interacting Majorana fermions on triangular-lattice ladders. Included among these phases is one in which symmetry-protected topological order coexists with spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our results indicate a mechanism through which interactions among Majorana modes generate nontrivial symmetry-fractionalized orders. These phases may be realized in arrays of vortex-bound Majorana zero modes on the surface of topological superconductors.

item.title: [7] Unusual critical currents in quasi-one-dimensional superconducting aluminum two-width structures in a magnetic field (V.I. Kuznetsov, O.V. Trofimov, Physica B)
item.description:
Last authors: V. I. Kuznetsov, O. V. Trofimov

Published as: V.I. Kuznetsov, O.V. Trofimov, Physica B DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of unusual critical currents in quasi-1D superconducting aluminum structures in a magnetic field.

Tags: #quasi-1D #superconductivity #transport #experimental

Abstract: We measured critical switching and retrapping currents as functions of temperature in the zero field and as functions of a magnetic field perpendicular to the substrate surface at a temperature close to the critical temperature in thin-film long quasi-one-dimensional superconducting aluminum two-width structures consisting of narrow and wide wires with different critical temperatures. It is found that the switching current as a function of the field is nonlocal (dependent on electron transport in the area containing the junction line between the narrow and wide wires). The unusual behavior of the switching current lies in the fact that it is poorly described by the classical Ginzburg-Landau theory. In low and intermediate fields, the switching current is determined mainly by the densities of critical currents in the narrow and wide wires, respectively, near the wire junction line. In high fields, the switching current is due to equilibrium fluctuations of the order parameter.

item.title: [8] Nonuniform superconducting states from Majorana flat bands (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer

Authors: Sushanth Varada, Aksel Kobia{\l}ka, Ankita Bhattacharya, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of nonuniform superconducting states arising from Majorana flat bands in topological superconductors.

Tags: #Majorana #topologicalsuperconductor #flatband #superconductivity #theory

Abstract: Zero-energy flat bands within the superconducting gap can give rise to competing ordered phases. We investigate such phases in topological superconductors based on the magnetic adatom platform hosting a flat band of Majorana edge states. Our self-consistent calculations of the superconducting order parameter show the emergence of both a pair density wave with edge-localized amplitude modulations, often a bond wave order, and a phase crystal characterized by longer-wavelength edge-localized phase modulations. Both these states lower the free energy by gapping out the Majorana flat band, but use different mechanisms tied to the underlying topology. In fact, at zero temperature the uniform superconducting solution with Majorana flat band never survives. Instead, a pair density wave appears when sufficient Majorana modes exist with oppositely signed topological winding numbers, while a phase crystal appears in regions of the phase diagram where one non-trivial winding number is heavily dominating. A crossover region connects these two states with modulations in both amplitude and phase. At finite temperatures, the pair density wave survives up to around 80% of the bulk superconducting transition temperature, while the phase crystal only appears at lower temperatures and the crossover region is also strongly suppressed. Our findings establish the ubiquity of emergent nonuniform superconducting phases and their temperature-dependent behavior in topological superconductors.

item.description:

Authors: Paulo Pires, Pierre-Paul De Breuck, Mauro Fava, Hai-Chen Wang, Miguel A. L. Marques

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Machine learning for materials property prediction using DFT-derived electronic structure (pDOS); relevant to superconductivity.

Abstract: Graph neural networks have become the dominant machine-learning architecture for predicting materials properties from crystal structures. item.title: [7] First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions (Phys. Rev. Mater.)
item.description:
Last authors: Feliciano Giustino, Young-Woo Son

Authors: Hong-Guk Min, Wooil Yang, Sabyasachi Tiwari, Feliciano Giustino, Young-Woo Son

Published as: Phys. Rev. Mater. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: First-principles study of electronic structure, transport, and optical properties in strained ZnO with Hubbard interactions.

Tags: #computational #electronicstructure #transport #oxides

Abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparency, and establish DFPT+U as an effective framework for predicting strain-dependent transport and optical properties in wide-band-gap oxides with implications for strain-engineered display and optoelectronic applications.

item.title: [8] Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals (Journal American Chemical Society (2026))
item.description:
Last authors: Kwanpyo Kim, Sunmin Ryu

Authors: Eunbeen Jeon, Kihyun Lee, Jieun Yeon, et al.

Published as: Journal American Chemical Society (2026) DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of exciton coupling in 2D organic-inorganic heterocrystals, relevant to 2D materials and heterostructures.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #heterostructures #excitons #spectroscopy

Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA's photoluminescence was completely quenched because of organic-to-inorganic hole transfer, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photoluminescence excitation spectroscopy, we found that the enhancement arises from two distinct mechanisms. Ground-state charge transfer injects holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. In addition, resonant energy transfer, enabled by spectral overlap between PTCDA and MoS2, diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. Our findings reconcile previously proposed mechanisms and establish a unified framework in which charge and energy transfer cooperate to govern exciton coupling at organic-inorganic interfaces.

item.title: [9] Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV2Se2O
item.description:
Last authors: Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinova

Authors: Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Colin Lange, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Links altermagnetism to photoemission spectroscopy in a real material, highly relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #altermagnetism #photoemission #electronicstructure #realmaterial

Abstract: We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in KV$_2$Se$_2$O. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry. These results are not only relevant for the metallic and room-temperature magnet KV$_2$Se$_2$O, but also for several other Lieb lattice systems. Our work expands the pool of techniques that can be used to detect altermagnetism emerging at the surfaces of antiferromagnets.

item.title: [10] Quetzalcoatlite as a Disorder-Free Platform for Chiral Magnetism and Frustration
item.description:
Last authors: Michael R. Norman, Roser Valent\'i

Authors: Aleksandar Razpopov, P. Peter Stavropoulos, Felix Flicker, Michael R. Norman, Roser Valent\'i

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ab initio study of a perfect kagome magnet revealing chiral magnetism and frustration, highly relevant.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #kagome #magnetism #electronicstructure #computational #chiral

Abstract: The natural mineral quetzalcoatlite Zn$_6$Cu$_3$(TeO$_6$)$_2$(OH)$_6$ $\cdot$ (Ag$_x$Pb$_y$Cl$_{x+2y}$) is a structurally ideal kagome magnet, providing a platform for exploring the interplay of geometric frustration, chirality, and tunability in a disorder-free framework. Here, we present the (first) comprehensive ab initio study of its electronic and magnetic properties. The electronic structure is dominated by localized half-filled Cu $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals that become insulating through electronic correlations. Mapping the low-energy physics onto a Heisenberg model reveals that the magnetism is governed primarily by two exchange interactions: a nearest-neighbor intralayer kagome coupling and a next-nearest-neighbor interlayer coupling. Their competition stabilizes an unconventional three-dimensional chiral magnetic state. Each kagome layer hosts a $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order, while adjacent layers are rotated by $60^\circ$, producing a right-handed spiral along the crystallographic $c$-axis. This intrinsic chiral order emerges naturally from the crystal structure and magnetic interactions, establishing quetzalcoatlite as a distinctive realization of chiral magnetism on a perfect kagome lattice. At the same time, the small energy scale of the exchange interactions places the material close to competing magnetic regimes, suggesting that moderate pressure, chemical substitution, or structural modifications may strongly enhance frustration, suppress long-range order, and potentially drive the system toward a quantum spin-liquid state.

item.title: [8] Electrically Switchable Spintronics in a Multiferroic Altermagnet
item.description:
Last authors: Universidad de Santiago de Chile, Alvaro S. Nunez (Departamento de F\'isica

Authors: Martin Latorre (Departamento de F\'isica, CEDENNA, FCFM, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical model for electrically switchable altermagnetism with direct implications for spintronics and transport.

Tags: #altermagnetism #spintronics #theory #multiferroic #transport

Abstract: We introduce a minimal model of a two-dimensional lattice that, upon spontaneous symmetry breaking, simultaneously develops altermagnetic order, a finite electric polarization, and a spin-polarized transport response, all of which are controlled by an external electric field. By coupling a dimerized altermagnet to an external electric field, we show that the three order parameters are not merely compatible but dynamically entangled, so that switching one (for instance, reversing the polarization with an electric field) necessarily reconfigures the other two. We show that this model offers a clear physical blueprint for designing next-generation spintronic logic and pure spin current memdevices that merge the ultrafast, stray-field-free advantages of compensated magnets with the low-power switching architectures of ferroelectrics.

item.title: [7] Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Polireddi Naveen, Abhiram Soori

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of Josephson effect in magnetic semiconductors with electrical control and anomalous effects; relevant to superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #Josephsoneffect #magneticsemiconductor #theory #spintronics

Abstract: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$\pi$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $\pi$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. This behavior originates from the intrinsic breaking of time-reversal symmetry associated with the spin-polarized electronic structure of the BMS. Interestingly, despite the simultaneous breaking of time-reversal and inversion symmetries---conditions often associated with nonreciprocal superconducting transport---we do not observe a Josephson diode effect. Our results therefore highlight an important distinction between anomalous Josephson transport and superconducting nonreciprocity: the former does not necessarily imply a finite critical-current asymmetry between opposite current directions.
