item.title: [7] Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI3 nanotubes
item.description:
Last authors: Braga, Portugal)

Authors: David Sanz (Universidad de Alicante, San Vicente del Raspeig, Spain), et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetic excitations in 2D materials are relevant for topological and magnetic systems research.

Tags: #magnon #CrI3 #magnetism

Abstract: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

item.title: [8] Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
item.description:
Last authors: Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu

Authors: Jing-Xuan Wang, Jia-Ming Wang, Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT+DMFT study of correlated layered materials relevant to cuprate/nickelate electronic structure comparisons.

Tags: #electronic-structure #correlated #DFT+DMFT

Abstract: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

item.title: [8] Moir\'e Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
item.description:
Last authors: Xi Dai, Chen Hu

Authors: Shiyu Peng, Yifan Wang, Peiyao Qin, Yixuan Liu, Xi Dai, Chen Hu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of moire Chern ferromagnets links closely to topological magnetic phases of interest.

Tags: #moire #topological #ferromagnet

Abstract: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moir\'e Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling {\nu}_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moir\'e Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

item.title: [8] Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La2SmNi2O7-
item.description:
Last authors: Junjie Zhang, Hai-Hu Wen

Authors: Yongze Ye, Feiyu Li, Di Peng, Junjie Zhang, Hai-Hu Wen

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of critical scaling and vortex dynamics in superconducting nickelates.

Tags: #material #superconductivity #experiment #nickelate

Abstract: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

item.title: [8] Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
item.description:
Last authors: E. Prada, S. Vaitiek\.{e}nas

Authors: D. Rana, O. S. Kurapati, N. Vanjarapu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic-superconducting nanowire hybrid junctions.

Tags: #experiment #superconductivity #ferromagnetism #material #nanowire #spintronics

Abstract: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

item.title: [9] Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe3Al2Si3O12
item.description:
Last authors: Harald O. Jeschke, Daniel Guterding

Authors: Minnong Zhang, Harald O. Jeschke, Daniel Guterding

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT and neutron scattering predictions for hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in a real material.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #material #magnetism #kagome #dft #neutronscattering #theory

Abstract: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$\~K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

item.title: [9] Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
item.description:
Last authors: J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

Authors: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance to Weyl semimetals, topological physics, and proposed experimental magnetoelectric effect.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #Weylsemimetals #topological #transport #magnetoelectricity #chiralanomaly

Abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

item.title: [7] Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
item.description:
Last authors: Niclas Westerberg, Robert Bennett

Authors: William S. McGregor, Niclas Westerberg, Robert Bennett

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical work on magneto-electric coupling in time-symmetry-broken topological insulators with experimental implications.

Tags: #topologicalinsulator #magneto-electriccoupling #time-reversalsymmetrybreaking #theoreticalcondensedmatter

Abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

Authors: Oleh Shtanko, Volodymyr Prokopenko, Oleksandr Prokopenko

Why: Theoretical study of spin Hall devices with antiferromagnetic layers, relevant to magnetic materials and spin transport.

Tags: #antiferromagnetism #spinHalleffect #spintronics #devicephysics #magneticmaterials

Abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

item.title: [8] Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
item.description:
Last authors: Torsten Ke{\ss}ler, Sergej Rjasanow

Authors: Andreas A. Buchheit, Torsten Ke{\ss}ler, Sergej Rjasanow

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Computational method for unconventional superconductors, identifying topological Weyl point nodes in 3D lattices.

Tags: #unconventionalsuperconductivity #Weylsemimetals #topological #computationalcondensedmatter #nodalsuperconductivity

Abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $\nu>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

item.title: [9] A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
item.description:
Last authors: In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park

Authors: Jong-Am Hong, Min-Jae Maeng, Kyu-Myung Lee, Seunggu Lee, In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: photoemission

Tags: #photoemission

Abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

item.title: [8] U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
item.description:
Last authors: Yang Zhong, Hongjun Xiang

Authors: Hongyu Yu, Yinze Hu, Yizhou Chen, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Computational model for spin-resolved Hamiltonians, Hubbard U, and altermagnetism, directly relevant to electronic structure.

Tags: #computationalmethod #electronicstructure #magnetism #altermagnetism #DFT+U

Abstract: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

item.title: [7] Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Zhijin Li, Tinghong Shen

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Theoretical study using CFT and QMC to understand quantum criticality in 2D quantum magnets.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #quantumcriticality #quantummagnets #theoreticalphysics #stronglycorrelatedelectrons

Abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $\phi$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $\Delta_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

item.title: [8] Quantum geometric spectroscopy with Schr\"odinger cat states
item.description:
Last authors: Shohei Imai, Marcelo F. Ciappina

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Proposes a new spectroscopic method to probe Berry curvature and quantum geometry of matter, directly relevant to user's interests.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #spectroscopy #quantumgeometry #Berrycurvature #experimentalmethod

Abstract: We propose a spectroscopic approach that reads out the quantum geometry of matter from the quantum decoherence of Schr\"{o}dinger-cat light, in the same way that optical absorption reads out the energy structure of matter. For a cat-state probe comprising a superposition of two coherent states, the interbranch coherence of the outgoing light encodes the overlap between the matter states driven by the two branches. We show that, when the electromagnetic fields of the two branches differ only slightly, cat-branch decoherence is quantified by dynamical quantum geometry, which characterizes infinitesimal displacements on the matter-state manifold. For frequency-selective kitten probes of equilibrium matter, we further establish a partition law for the quantum geometric tensor between light and matter, enabling optical readout of matter quantum metric and Berry curvature through, for example, the brightening of a stellar zero in the outgoing Husimi function. For nonequilibrium matter in a pure state, short-pulse cat probes also provide a time-resolved witness of multipartite entanglement through the transient quantum metric, which can be extracted from homodyne measurements of the outgoing light. By turning cat-state decoherence, conventionally regarded as a loss of quantum information, into a carrier of information about matter, this approach establishes a spectroscopic principle that directly probes quantum-state geometry and fluctuations alongside conventional response-based spectroscopy.

item.title: [7] Cavity Control of Emission Dynamics from Spin Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
item.description:
Last authors: Sven H\"ofling, Simon Betzold

Authors: Anuj Kumar Singh, Atanu Patra, Paul Konrad, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin defects in hBN 2D material, relevant for quantum applications.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #spindefects #hBN #quantummaterials #optics #experiment

Abstract: Optically addressable negatively charged boron vacancy ($\mathrm{V_B^-}$) defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are promising for quantum sensing at room temperature. The two-dimensional structure of hBN allows direct access to the local environment, enabling proximal sensing of target materials. However, its broadband emission and low quantum yield hinder efficient light-matter interaction, and the coupling of $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ optical dipoles to confined cavity fields remains poorly understood. In this study, we integrate $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defects with a tunable plano-concave microcavity, achieving three-dimensional optical confinement. This approach yields photoluminescence (PL) enhancement and cavity-modified optical decay dynamics, providing insights into the orientation of the $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defect dipole. Time-resolved PL measurements identify a distinct fast decay component, suggesting a complex dipole geometry for the defects. Therefore, a tilted optical dipole model is considered to attribute the fast and slow decay components to in-plane and out-of-plane dipole contributions, respectively. Additionally, optically detected magnetic resonance and excitation-polarisation-dependent PL measurements provide further insights into local symmetry breaking and potential optical dipole configurations. These results highlight the role of optical dipole orientation in $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defect-cavity coupling.

item.title: [8] Genuine multipartite entanglement in ring-shaped Hubbard models
item.description:
Last authors: R. Di Felice, F. Troiani

Authors: K. Shahzad, S. Pittalis, G. Goldoni, R. Di Felice, F. Troiani

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of Hubbard models connecting entanglement to charge-density waves.

Tags: #theory #Hubbardmodel #stronglycorrelated #CDW #entanglement

Abstract: Spin states can be extracted from many-electron systems by detecting electrons at a set of lattice sites, which act as particle labels. Here we quantify the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) of such spin states, which are generally mixed, in standard and extended Hubbard rings, together with the corresponding detection probability. We show that the on-site repulsion, by suppressing charge fluctuations, enhances the GME, and that in the strongly interacting regime at half filling the detection probability decreases only weakly with the number of spins. The GME is robust at temperatures below the singlet--triplet gap, and can even be enhanced by doping, in spite of the induced charge fluctuations. The transition from spin- to charge-density waves in the extended Hubbard model is signaled by an abrupt suppression of both the GME and the detection probability.

item.title: [9] Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial -Sb on Al(111)
item.description:
Last authors: Yang Wang, Pujing Zhang

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Experimental STM/STS/photoemission study on emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial Sb.

Tags: #STM/STS #photoemission #kagome #electronicstructure #spinHall

Abstract: We report the epitaxial growth of $\beta$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $\beta$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $\beta$-Sb. For a reference $\beta$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

item.title: [8] Orbital antiferromagnetic currents in a frustrated fermionic ladder (Eur. Phys. J. B)
item.description:
Last authors: G. I. Japaridze, A. A. Nersesyan

Authors: Shota Garuchava, G. I. Japaridze, A. A. Nersesyan

Published as: Eur. Phys. J. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of frustrated fermionic ladder showing orbital antiferromagnetic currents and TRSB.

Tags: #theory #quasi-1D #Hubbard #frustration #TRSB #antiferromagnetism

Abstract: We consider a spinless $t$-$t'$ ionic Hubbard chain at 1/2 filling and large hopping ratio $t'/t$. In this limit the model adequately maps onto a weakly coupled triangular ladder with a potential interchain bias. The low-energy properties of the system are formed due to the interplay of geometrical frustration, correlations and charge imbalance. We derive the effective field-theoretical model to study universal properties of the model in the scaling limit. We show that at full dynamical frustration the ground state of the ladder represents a repulsive version of the Luther-Emery liquid with dominant orbital antiferromagnetic correlations exhibiting the slowest power-law decay in the ground state. Pairing correlations also display algebraic order but are subdominant. At an incomplete dynamical frustration a finite commensurability gap is dynamically generated, and the fluctuating OAF transforms to a long-range ordered state with a spontaneously broken time reversal symmetry. The mass gap in the spectrum of relative density fluctuations gets suppressed upon increasing the potential bias.

item.title: [7] Easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB2 at low temperatures
item.description:
Last authors: Ulrich Zeitler, Christian Pfleiderer

Authors: Christoph Resch, Georg Benka, Andreas Bauer, Elvina Dilmieva, Ulrich Zeitler, Christian Pfleiderer

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental characterization of easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB2.

Tags: #material #magnetism #ferromagnetism #characterization #transport

Abstract: We report a study of high-quality single crystals of the hexagonal rare-earth diboride ErB$_{2}$ prepared by means of the self-adjusted flux travelling-solvent floating-zone technique. Comprehensive measurements of the ac susceptibility, magnetization, specific heat, and electrical resistivity consistently establish a paramagnetic state at room temperature which develops strong easy-plane magnetic anisotropy of the hexagonal basal plane below a temperature $T_{\rm x} \approx 50$~K. Below a pronounced second-order phase transition at $T_{c} = 14$~K long-range magnetic order stabilizes. Excellent agreement with both the qualitative phenomenology and the quantitative characteristics of the thermodynamic and transport properties under applied magnetic fields up to 30\,T identifies the magnetic order in ErB$_2$ as a showcase par excellence of pronounced easy-plane ferromagnetism of Er$^{3+}$ local moments, in the presence of crystal electric fields and Van Vleck contributions.

item.title: [8] Nonreciprocal Shapiro steps in Josephson diodes
item.description:
Last authors: Qiang-Hua Wang, Congjun Wu

Authors: Da Wang, Qiang-Hua Wang, Congjun Wu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on nonreciprocal Shapiro steps in Josephson diodes, with implications for TRSB experiments.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #TRSB #Josephsoneffect

Abstract: Various microscopic mechanisms have been proposed for the Josephson diode effect, which are unified phenomenologically within a nonreciprocal resistively and capacitively shunted junction model. We further systematically investigate the dynamical response of these Josephson diodes to radio-frequency AC driving current, focusing in particular on the nonreciprocity of Shapiro steps. We show that the Shapiro step structures encode the information about the underlying diode mechanisms in both overdamped and noised underdamped junctions. In particular, we propose the zero-voltate step center as a fingerprint of different Josephson diode mechanisms in the overdamped regime, which is captured analytically within a harmonic approximation for small AC amplitudes. Our results provides a route to experimentally distinguish different Josephson diode mechanisms, including those with and without time-reversal symmetry breaking.

item.title: [7] Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian (Annals of Physics)
item.description:
Last authors: Klaus Ziegler

Published as: Annals of Physics DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on topological pseudospin order and edge modes in 2D superconductors, relevant to topological superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #topological #theory #edgestates

Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.

item.title: [9] Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr2SeO
item.description:
Last authors: Haiming Duan, Fangping Ouyang

Authors: Yunfei Gao, Aolin Li, Zesen Fu, Bei Zhang, Haiming Duan, Fangping Ouyang

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct relevance to altermagnetism and electric-field control in Cr2SeO, predicting experimental transport and Kerr effect.

Tags: #altermagnetism #spintronics #DFT #transport #magneticmaterials

Abstract: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for spintronics by combining zero net magnetization with nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet efficient electrical manipulation of their spin-dependent transport remains challenging. Here, using first-principles calculations, we show that an out-of-plane electric field induces spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO, gives rise to a magneto-optical Kerr effect, and drives a semiconductor-to-metal transition at sufficiently high field magnitudes. Reversing the field direction switches the spin-momentum-locking pattern, which reverses the sign of the Kerr rotation angle as well as that of the longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Leveraging this electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking, we propose a dual-gate altermagnetic tunnel junction in which high- and low-resistance states are realized without reversing the N\'eel vector. The resistance switching originates from the matching and mismatching of spin-polarized conducting channels in momentum space, yielding a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio on the order of $10^{8}$. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for realizing electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO and developing all-electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronic devices.

item.title: [8] A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems
item.description:
Last authors: Mengxing Ye

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Advanced many-body theory for orbital magnetism and Berry curvature in correlated multiband electron systems.

Tags: #theory #stronglycorrelated #orbitalmagnetism #Berrycurvature #Luttinger-Ward

Abstract: Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of $B$ applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.

item.title: [8] Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
item.description:
Last authors: Vladimir P. Mineev

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb, directly relevant to electronic structure and altermagnetism.

Tags: #altermagnetism #bandstructure #theory #CrSb

Abstract: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

item.title: [9] Linear response of the Chern insulator MnBi2Te4: A Wannier function approach
item.description:
Last authors: Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Sipe

Authors: Matthew Albert, Javier Sivianes, Jason G. Kattan, Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Sipe

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Computational study of electronic structure, Chern number, and optical response in magnetic topological MnBi2Te4.

Tags: #topological #Cherninsulator #MnBi2Te4 #electronicstructure #DFT #transport

Abstract: Recent work demonstrated that in the long wavelength limit the linear response of a Chern insulator to finite-frequency electric fields is the sum of two terms: A general frequency-dependent Kubo contribution that is present irrespective of band topology, and a topological Hall term that vanishes for topologically trivial insulators. Motivated by recent experiments and theoretical predictions, we use these expressions to calculate the optical conductivity and susceptibility of intrinsically magnetic MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin films with one, four, five, and eleven septuple layers by combining density functional theory with "single-shot" Wannier functions. To characterize the underlying topology of these systems, we compute the two-dimensional Chern number of these films using recently derived global expressions formulated in terms of Bloch energies and velocity matrix elements; the use of these expressions allows us to circumvent numerical issues at band crossings. Films with eleven septuple layers are of particular interest. We find that they have the same Chern number as five septuple layer films, in contrast to the reported "higher Chern-number phase" of these systems in other studies; we discuss a few possible reasons for the discrepancy. A layer-resolved decomposition of the static reactive susceptibility reveals a non-uniform spatial distribution, with interlayer contributions dominating over intralayer contributions and the bulk layers accounting for nearly 70% of the total response. We also identify spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversions as a possible indicator of these topological phases.

item.title: [9] Quantum-Geometric Spin Magnetization and Spin Currents Across Altermagnetic Symmetry Classes
item.description:
Last authors: Snehasish Nandy, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh

Authors: Neelanjan Chakraborti, Snehasish Nandy, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on quantum-geometric spin responses in altermagnets, involving Berry curvature, band structure, and experimental probes.

Tags: #altermagnetism #Berrycurvature #quantumgeometry #spincurrent #transport #bandstructure #theory

Abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split band structures despite vanishing equilibrium spin magnetization, making field-induced responses a direct probe of their quantum geometry. Based on symmetry, altermagnets can be classified into M-, S-, A-, and S/A-type according to the presence or absence of inversion and time-reversal symmetries. We develop a unified framework using a generalized quantum geometric tensor that captures both momentum translations and spin rotations of Bloch states. In particular, we introduce the Zeeman counterpart of the conventional spin quantum geometric tensor, whose real and imaginary parts define the Zeeman spin quantum metric and Zeeman spin Berry curvature, respectively. Using this framework, we study linear spin magnetization and spin currents induced by electric and magnetic fields. We show that M- and S-type altermagnets support intrinsic electric-field-induced spin currents and magnetic-field-induced spin magnetization, while A-type altermagnets exhibit both electric and magnetic field induced spin current and spin magnetization. For S/A-type altermagnets, neither inversion nor time-reversal symmetry alone determines the allowed responses. Applying our theory to the S-type $d$-wave altermagnet $\mathrm{FeSb}_2$ and a Rashba-coupled S/A-type $d$-wave altermagnet, we find complete agreement with the symmetry constraints. The predicted responses are sizable and within reach of magnetometry and spin-transport experiments. Our results establish a symmetry based quantum geometric framework for spin responses in altermagnets and highlight their potential for experimental detection and spintronic applications.

item.title: [8] Probing PbTe-Pb nanowire devices with radio-frequency reflectometry
item.description:
Last authors: Ke He, Hao Zhang

Authors: Xin-Yi Tang, Lin Li, Zezhou Xia, et al.

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental work on PbTe-Pb nanowires, a real material system for probing Majorana zero modes.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #Majorana #topological #nanowire #experiment #PbTe-Pb

Abstract: We report the implementation of radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry on selective-area-grown PbTe-Pb nanowire devices on a CdTe substrate. These nanowires are predicted to host Majorana zero modes. We demonstrate the compatibility of the rf technique, including both resistive and capacitive sensing, with these nanowires. The effect of dielectric loss from the CdTe substrate is quantitatively characterized. Furthermore, the feasibility of rf reflectometry is verified under finite magnetic fields where zero-energy modes can emerge. Our results establish the fast control of PbTe quantum devices, paving the way for their applications in topological quantum computation.

item.title: [8] Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in PT antiferromagnets
item.description:
Last authors: K. D. Belashchenko

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of surface altermagnetism in antiferromagnets, relevant for transport and experimental probes.

Tags: #altermagnetism #antiferromagnetism #surface #transport #theory

Abstract: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

item.title: [7] Quantum sensing of weak ferromagnetism in a phase-separated Mn-doped CaFe3O5
item.description:
Last authors: J. Paul Attfield, Denis Ar\v{c}on

Authors: Izidor Benedi\v{c}i\v{c}, J. Paul Attfield, Denis Ar\v{c}on

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnetism and phase separation in a correlated oxide using quantum magnetometry.

Tags: #experiment #magnetism #stronglycorrelated #phasetransition #oxides #quantumsensing

Abstract: Doping of transition metal oxides such as CaFe$_3$O$_5$ offers a controlled way to tune the interplay of charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom, yet local-probe studies remain difficult because strong correlations and dynamic charge-spin fluctuations obscure fine spectroscopic features in powder samples. Here, we employ quantum magnetometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in nanodiamonds impressed into an Mn-doped CaFe$_3$O$_5$ powder pellet to probe static and dynamic magnetic fields across the weak ferromagnetic transition. The splitting and broadening of the optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra exhibit an order-parameter-like increase by $\sim 15 ~{\rm MHz}$ upon cooling below the critical temperature, $T_{\rm c}$. Concomitantly, the spin-lattice relaxation rate, $1/T_1$, exhibits a pronounced enhancement at $T_\mathrm{c}$, increasing approximately fivefold from its high-temperature value. Moreover, detailed lineshape fits of ODMR spectra together with the stretched-exponential NV magnetization recovery curves corroborate the proposed electronic phase segregation in charge-ordered and charge-averaged phases at the microscale. The presented study demonstrates the viability of using nanodiamonds as a platform for local magnetic probing of strongly correlated matter, including phenomena such as electronic phase separation.

item.title: [10] Interface-Confined Superconductivity with Thickness-Independent Superfluid Stiffness in (Pb,Sn)Te/FeTe Bilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Chih-Kang Shih, Cui-Zu Chang

Authors: Zi-Jie Yan, Hongtao Rong, Yiyuan Luo, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: ARPES study of interface-confined topological superconductivity and Dirac states, relevant to Majorana.

Tags: #ARPES #superconductivity #topological #Majorana #Dirac #heterostructure #experiment

Abstract: Interface-induced superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures provides a promising route toward topological superconductivity, yet the roles of the neighboring layers topology, symmetry, and electronic structure remain unresolved. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to track the evolution of the Pb1-xSnxTe layer from a trivial insulator to a topological crystalline insulator hosting multiple Dirac surface states. Electrical transport measurements reveal robust superconductivity throughout the entire composition range, with a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature of ~12 K despite substantial changes in the electronic structure and topology of Pb1-xSnxTe. Double-coil mutual-inductance measurements further reveal comparable superfluid stiffness across the topological phase transition and nearly thickness-independent superfluid stiffness despite large variations in the constituent-layer thicknesses, demonstrating that superconductivity is confined near the interface. These results establish that superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures is largely insensitive to the topology, crystal symmetry, and detailed electronic structure of the neighboring layer, supporting a primary origin in modifications to the FeTe layer. The coexistence of interface-confined superconductivity and tunable multiple Dirac surface states in Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers provides a versatile platform for exploring topological superconductivity and interactions among multiple Majorana zero modes.

item.title: [8] Electronic and magnetic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals from an ab initio approach
item.description:
Last authors: Daniele Lagasco, Jan Arjan Berger

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ab initio study of electronic/magnetic properties in quasi-1D Wigner crystals, relevant to user's 1D material interests.

Tags: #1Dmaterials #Wignercrystal #abinitio #electronicstructure #magnetism #carbonnanotubes #theory

Abstract: We present an ab initio method to study the electronic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. In particular, we focus on the calculation of the electronic charge distribution. Our theoretical studies are motivated by the experimental observation of few-electron Wigner crystals in a carbon nanotube [Science 364, 870 (2019)]. We model the experimental setup by confining electrons in a one-dimensional potential well with hard-wall boundary conditions. We represent the Hamiltonian of the system in a basis of Slater determinants and perform full configuration interaction to ensure we capture all the electron correlation for a given basis set. As the one-particle basis set we use particle-in-a-box wave functions which by construction satisfy the boundary conditions. With our approach, we obtain accurate electronic density profiles of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. These profiles clearly show the localisation of the electrons. Moreover, we calculate the exchange coupling constant of the Wigner dimer by mapping our ab initio method on a Heisenberg Hamiltonian. We obtain a reasonable agreement with a result in the literature.

item.title: [8] Proximity effects of chiral magnetization on transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers
item.description:
Last authors: Igor S. Krivenko, Dmitry S. Smirnov

Authors: Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Igor S. Krivenko, Dmitry S. Smirnov

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of anomalous Hall effect and chiral magnetism in TMD monolayers with experimental implications.

Tags: #monolayer #TMD #antiferromagnetism #anomalousHalleffect #proximityeffect #theory #transport #optics

Abstract: We consider the proximity effects of a commensurate chiral $120^{\circ}$ N\'eel magnetic structure on the transport and optical properties of a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer (TMD ML). The enlarged magnetic unit cell leads to the folding of the Brillouin zone and enables efficient intervalley spin-flip scattering. Starting from a six band tight binding model, we develop an effective $k\cdot p$ model, which describes the coupling between charge carriers in the TMD ML and the chiral magnetization. We predict the anomalous antiferromagnetic Hall effect (AHE) for conduction electrons and describe it accounting for the interplay between anomalous velocity, side jump, and skew scattering contributions. The proximity of the chiral magnetization also leads to the mixing and splitting of the exciton resonances in the two valleys which are related by the time reversal symmetry despite zero net magnetization. Finally, we demonstrate the possibility to measure the distribution of in-plane orientation of the chiral magnetization through Faraday rotation and the ellipticity of incident linearly polarized light.

item.title: [8] Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
item.description:
Last authors: Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov

Authors: Igor S. Krivenko, Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of valley-controlled chiral magnetism and RKKY in TMD monolayers, relevant to 2D materials and QSLs.

Tags: #monolayer #TMD #vanderWaals #heterostructure #magnetism #RKKY #quantumspinliquid #theory

Abstract: We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.

item.title: [9] Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission /T scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
item.description:
Last authors: Jian Xian Sim

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: photoemission

Tags: #ARPES #photoemission #cuprate #quantumcritical

Abstract: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $\omega/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_{\alpha}(r) \sim 1/r^\alpha$, with doping-dependent $\alpha$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $\gamma$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $\alpha$, as $\gamma = 2-\frac{1}{\alpha}$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $\omega/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.

item.title: [7] Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko

Authors: Tony Liu, Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of nonreciprocal effects and diode efficiency in noncentrosymmetric Rashba superconductors.

Tags: #superconductivity #noncentrosymmetric #RashbaSOC #transport #theory #Ginzburg-Landau

Abstract: We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. On the thermodynamic side we construct the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the linear and cubic gradient terms and the momentum-odd part of the quartic vertex, and trace their dependence on disorder. The couplings of the quadratic sector are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature. It interpolates between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles known results for the magnetoelectric couplings of disordered Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $q$, and hence the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $q$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise change together, so that equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the relaxation dynamics becomes nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with higher-gradient terms, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient. We also consider fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, which grows as the inverse square of the distance to $T_c$ and is suppressed in the relaxation-dominated regime.

item.title: [7] Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
item.description:
Last authors: Kenji Watanabe, Feng Wang

Authors: Ha-Leem Kim, Hyungbin Lim, Yuanyi Yang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental technique for spatially resolved transport in 2D semiconductors and vdW heterostructures, relevant to correlated states.

Tags: #experimentaltechnique #2Dmaterials #vanderWaals #transport #correlatedelectrons

Abstract: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local voltage into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances of a few k$\Omega$ despite M$\Omega$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. The optically derived resistance exhibits a metal-insulator crossover, and the voltage maps and reconstructed local conductivity reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in both insulating and metallic regimes. Beyond resolving channel resistance under high contact-resistance conditions, the technique provides spatially resolved access to microscopic transport heterogeneity in functional van der Waals devices.

item.title: [8] Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in p-wave antialtermagnets
item.description:
Last authors: Kristian M{\ae}land, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on spin-current effects in p-wave antialtermagnets, a directly relevant topic for the user.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #magnons #spincurrent

Abstract: We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.

item.title: [7] Spin-Exchange Induced Confinement of Correlated Bound States in the Continuum
item.description:
Last authors: Zhongming Gu, Jie Zhu

Authors: Kai Chen, Junyan Guan, Zhongming Gu, Jie Zhu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental observation of correlated bound states in the 1D Fermi-Hubbard model, relevant to strongly correlated electrons.

Tags: #experimental #stronglycorrelatedelectrons #Hubbardmodel #bandstructure #1Dsystems

Abstract: Repulsively bound doublons are two-particle composites formed by strong interactions and are usually separated from the scattering continuum. Introducing spin-exchange coupling (SEC) fundamentally alters the underlying band structure, providing a powerful tuning knob to shift these isolated pairs toward this continuum. However, because entering such a regime typically dictates immediate dissociation, whether this coupling can drive these pairs inside while preserving their bound nature constitutes a fundamental unresolved challenge. Here we show that spin-exchange coupling in the one-dimensional extended Fermi-Hubbard model can drive doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum. Most of these states hybridize with extended channels and decay, whereas a subset remains decoupled and spatially bound, forming many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs). We map the interacting two-particle problem onto a two-dimensional lattice of coupled acoustic cavities, and experimentally observe both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states. These results demonstrate that spin-exchange coupling can turn selected doublons into interaction-induced BICs, deepening the understanding of continuum physics for interaction-bound pairs.

item.title: [7] When the electrons go marching in: Resonances and accuracy of pairwise approximations in multiterminal Josephson junctions
item.description:
Last authors: A. Bar{\i}\c{s} \"Ozg\"uler

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical analysis of multiterminal Josephson junctions, relevant to superconductivity and quantum devices.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #Josephsonjunctions

Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions connect three or more superconductors through a common weak link. We quantify when their equilibrium currents admit a pairwise description. Multiterminal irreducible harmonics are energy components that depend jointly on three or more terminal phases and cannot be reduced to a sum of pair couplings. In microscopic planar-junction models, pairwise terms can capture nearly all energy variation while leaving appreciable current errors: phase differentiation amplifies the omitted harmonics. A terminal-independent Fourier projection quantifies this effect while allowing arbitrary nonsinusoidal pair couplings. Shared normal-region resonances provide a means of controlling the error. Selecting a mode from normal-state data and shifting it with a gate while retaining a frozen background reproduces the normalized error trends in the tested devices; prediction of the complete current waveform also depends on the background contribution. Finite-gap calculations retain the gate dependence at substantially lower absolute currents. An analytic single-level model supplies a sufficient detuning for pairwise accuracy. Together, these results connect normal-resonance control to a quantitative, current-based criterion for pairwise modeling.

item.title: [9] Ultra-small-angle graphene twistronics with monolayer spacers: From interlayer hybridisation and moir\'e effects to high-temperature magnetotransport oscillations
item.description:
Last authors: Vladimir I. Falko, Xiao Li

Authors: Benjamin Fuller, Haowei Fan, Agustin Montemurro, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical predictions for moire effects and magnetotransport in twisted graphene/hBN heterostructures, highly relevant to user's interests.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #theory #graphene #twistedbilayer #moire #vanderWaals #transport #magnetotransport

Abstract: Based on the analysis of moir\'e superlattice characteristics and interlayer hybridisation in small-angle twisted graphene multilayers with a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer, we predict spectral features and quantum transport effects in these systems. Here, we consider both a twisted bilayer and double bilayers with a spacer, discuss double bilayers in two stacking orders - with and without inversion symmetry - and also compare the results obtained with self-consistent Hartree calculations with and without in-plane periodic charge distribution, offering computationally efficient models for these graphene/hBN/graphene moir\'e systems. We note parametric intervals where the appearance of minibands can be enhanced by tuning with an out-of-plane displacement field, and identify the miniband edges and van Hove singularities across a broad range of densities and displacement fields. These system host Lifshitz transitions at which the Fermi lines form a network across moir\'e Brillouin zones, and to which Brown-Zak oscillations converge at low magnetic field and elevated temperatures. We analyse interlayer hybridisation across the same parameter space, discuss how hybridisation affects in-plane magneto-transport in ultra-high-mobility structures, and predict that semiclassical magneto-oscillations of interlayer hybridisation can lead to 1/B-periodic quantum oscillations of resistivity persistent to high temperature.

item.title: [9] Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La3Ni2O7 via 139La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the Am2m Structure (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.)
item.description:
Last authors: Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda

Authors: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, et al.

Published as: J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. DOI

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental NQR study of spin-stripe SDW order in nickelate La3Ni2O7, directly relevant to unconventional superconductivity.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #experimental #unconventionalsuperconductivity #nickelates #SDW #NQR #stronglycorrelatedelectrons

Abstract: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

item.title: [8] Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.)
item.description:
Last authors: Toshihito Osada

Published as: J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on transport and Fermi surface in Weyl/Dirac semimetals, relevant to experimental observables.

Tags: #theory #topological #Weylsemimetal #transport

Abstract: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.

item.title: [8] Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly relevant to topological semimetals and Berry curvature with proposed experimental nonlinear Hall signatures.

Tags: #theory #Diracsemimetal #topology

Abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

item.title: [7] Why "quantum spin liquids" are quantum singlet liquids
item.description:
Last authors: Sergey Syzranov, Arthur P. Ramirez

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Broadly important discussion on the nature and experimental signatures of quantum spin liquids.

Tags: #theory #spinliquid #magnetism

Abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, the theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm with theoretical arguments the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character in materials with half-integer spins per primitive magnetic cell. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

item.title: [8] Raman optical activity and helicity-dependent phonon splitting in chiral CoSi
item.description:
Last authors: Yoshihiko Togawa, Takuya Satoh

Authors: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates structural chirality and phonons in topological semimetal CoSi using helicity-dependent Raman scattering.

Tags: #CoSi #topologicalsemimetal #Raman #chiralphonons

Abstract: Circularly polarized Raman scattering in solids provides access to two distinct phenomena: Raman optical activity (ROA), an intensity difference between circular polarization channels, and helicity-dependent frequency splitting of chiral phonons. We observe both in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi and show that they arise through two different symmetry channels, each rendering phonon components with opposite crystal angular momenta inequivalent. Doubly degenerate E phonons exhibit a large ROA, with an approximately fourfold intensity contrast between the two cross-circular channels. The sign of this ROA reverses between the front and back {111} surfaces, while its strong suppression on {110} supports the assignment to the axial electric toroidal octupole. By contrast, triply degenerate T phonons show helicity-dependent frequency splittings, whose mode-dependent signs are reproduced by the calculated dispersion of branches with opposite crystal angular momenta, thus identifying structural chirality as their source. First-principles calculations yield a pronounced E-mode intensity asymmetry in the resonant regime, reproduce the mode-dependent signs of the T-mode splittings, and account for their magnitudes within approximately 40%. These results establish circularly polarized Raman scattering as a symmetry- and angular-momentum-resolved probe of chiral and axial multipolar symmetry in solids.

item.title: [7] Quadrupole Origin of the Orbital Hall Effect in an sp3 Centrosymmetric Lattice: Robustness and Tunability under Disorder
item.description:
Last authors: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Henrique P. Veiga, Aur\'elien Manchon, Tatiana G. Rappoport

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Discusses orbital Hall transport and electronic structure theory relevant to topological phenomena.

Tags: #Halleffect #transport #electronic-structure

Abstract: We investigate how disorder affects orbital Hall transport in the centrosymmetric spinless $sp^3$ tight-binding model on a square lattice, widely used as a minimal model for the orbital Hall effect [1]. In the pristine system, the intrinsic orbital Hall response is related to the quadrupolar orbital texture generated by $s$-$p$ hybridization. Using the Kubo-Bastin formalism expanded in Chebyshev polynomials, we analyze the effect of vacancies, orbital-dependent Anderson on-site disorder, and selective $V_{sp\sigma}$-bond disorder on the orbital transport. For Anderson disorder and vacancies, the longitudinal charge conductivity decreases faster than the orbital Hall conductivity over the range studied, leading to an increase of the orbital Hall angle and, in the Anderson case, saturation at stronger disorder. Selective $V_{sp\sigma}$-bond disorder behaves differently: by modifying only the $s$-$p$ hybridization channel while leaving the remaining hopping network intact, it can produce a non-monotonic orbital Hall response and enhance the orbital Hall conductivity at intermediate dilution. Overall, our results show that the orbital Hall response remains sizable under vacancy and on-site disorder, while selective modification of the $s$-$p$ hybridization provides an additional route to tune the orbital Hall conductivity.
