item.title: [7] Inversion of magnetization anisotropy in low magnetic fields for textured Bi2223 superconductor due to magnetic responses from superconducting crystallites and intercrystalline boundaries (J. Supercond Nov Magn.)
item.description:
Last authors: D. A. Balaev, S. V. Semenov, D. M. Gokhfeld, M. I. Petrov

Published as: J. Supercond Nov Magn. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetization studies on high-Tc superconductors.

Tags: #superconductivity #magnetism

Abstract: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference {\Delta}M between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H {\perp} NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H {\perp} NTP. Therefore, when the field is oriented H||NTP, a larger external field is required for magnetic flux to penetrate into the sample inner than for the H {\perp} NTP orientation.

item.title: [7] Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Yan S. Zha, Satoru Hayami

Authors: Cong Guan, Yan S. Zha, Satoru Hayami

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to topological magnetic structures in noncentrosymmetric magnets.

Tags: #magnetism #skyrmions

Abstract: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-$Q$ magnetic states.

item.description:

Tags: #topological #electronicstructure #bismuth

Abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

item.title: [7] Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Quantum Geometric Effects
item.description:
Last authors: Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie

Authors: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of exciton magnetic moment in bilayer graphene, connects to quantum geometry and experiment.

Tags: #theory #graphene #quantumgeometry #magnetism

Abstract: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.

item.title: [7] Hybrid light-matter boundaries of graphene in a chiral cavity
item.description:
Last authors: Volker Karle, Oriana K. Diessel, Vasil Rokaj, Ceren B. Da\u{g}

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on graphene in a chiral cavity, predicting chiral edge modes and hybrid band topology with experimental signatures.

Tags: #theory #graphene #topological #light-matterinteraction

Abstract: We establish the bulk-boundary correspondence for graphene in a circularly polarized cavity. Using exact diagonalization, transfer-matrix analysis, and introducing the Dirac-Jaynes-Cummings model, we identify chiral edge modes in the light-matter hybridization gaps, some bright with finite photon number. Particularly, analytical expressions are derived for the localization length and mode velocity of bright edge modes. Density matrix renormalization group on hybrid electron-photon tensors reveals that these gaps survive at finite electron density, leading to the first non-perturbative study of graphene in a chiral cavity, and connecting single- and many-electron pictures. We find that the time evolution converts dark edge states into bright unidirectional currents, which can provide an experimental signature of hybrid band topology, in addition to the many-body charge gaps.

item.title: [8] Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
item.description:
Last authors: Marvin L. Cohen, Timur Bazhirov

Authors: Vsevolod Biryukov, Sergey V. Barabash, Pranab Kumar Das, et al.

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: New AI-native DFT engine for quantum materials modeling; highly relevant computational methodology.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #DFT #computational #methodology #AI

Abstract: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.

item.title: [7] Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
item.description:
Last authors: Archishman Gupta, Ankit Arora

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ab initio study of strain-dependent electronic and thermal properties in a 2D material, silicene.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #DFT #phonon #transport #silicene

Abstract: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

item.title: [7] Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the MoS2/Sapphire System
item.description:
Last authors: Simon R. Phillpot, Youping Chen

Authors: Emir Bilgili, Nicholas Taormina, Simon R. Phillpot, Youping Chen

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Machine learning interatomic potential for MoS2/sapphire heterostructure, relevant to 2D materials and computation.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #vanderWaalsheterostructures #computational #methodology #MoS2 #phonon

Abstract: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the MoS$_2$/ $\alpha$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) system. The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from ~1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On 2,820 held-out test structures from the DFT pool, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/angstrom. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5 %, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of point defects (Spearman $\rho$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($\rho$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($\rho$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %.

item.title: [7] An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants (Nat. Commun.)
item.description:
Last authors: Hao Zhang, Matthew Otten

Published as: Nat. Commun. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Novel computational method for accurate electronic ground states in strongly correlated systems and real compounds.

Tags: #computational #electronicstructure #stronglycorrelated #methodology

Abstract: Accurate quantum many-body calculations often depend on reliable reference states or good human-designed ans\"atze, yet such knowledge can become unreliable in hard problems like strongly correlated systems. Here we show that high-accuracy many-body ground states can be discovered directly from random Slater determinants. We introduce the Trimmed Configuration Interaction (TrimCI) method, which self-refines by iteratively expanding and trimming configurations in the variational space. TrimCI matches state-of-the-art accuracy using orders of magnitude fewer determinants and computer time: $10^6$-fold fewer than a recent quantum computing calculation on an iron-sulfur cluster, $10^5$-fold fewer than a leading classical method on a larger iron-sulfur cluster in nitrogenase, and over 99% of the ground-state energy of a strongly correlated lattice system from $10^{-28}$ of its Hilbert space, exceeding quantum Monte Carlo accuracy by orders of magnitude in some regimes. TrimCI thus provides an auto-initializing, accurate and highly efficient framework for quantum many-body systems, whose compact explicit wavefunctions enable direct and rapid evaluation of observables.

item.title: [8] Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Eugene Demler, Andrea Cavalleri

Authors: Albert Liu, Danica Pavicevic, Alex G\'omez Salvador, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental work probing phase fluctuations in cuprate superconductors using advanced spectroscopy.

Tags: #cuprates #superconductivity #spectroscopy #experimental

Abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.

item.title: [7] Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
item.description:
Last authors: Subir Sachdev

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical work on fundamental Fermi surface properties in Fermi and fractionalized Fermi liquids.

Tags: #Fermisurface #Luttingerliquid #spinliquid #theory #electronicstructure

Abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $\rho$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $\rho$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $\rho -1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

item.title: [8] Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moir\'e Systems
item.description:
Last authors: Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales

Authors: Conor Smith, Yubo Yang, Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study predicting tunable charge order and quantum Hall in relevant moiré systems.

Tags: #moire #CDW #quantumHall #topological #theory #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moir\'e superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $\nu_B=1$ in the presence of a moir\'e superlattice potential, with three electrons per moir\'e cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moir\'e bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moir\'e minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a N\'eel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

item.title: [7] Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
item.description:
Last authors: Anton V. Zasedatelev, Martin Esmann

Authors: Jens-Christian Drawer, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Bo Han, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnon-phonon-polariton interactions in a van der Waals antiferromagnet.

Tags: #vanderWaals #antiferromagnetism #magnon #phonon #spectroscopy #experimental

Abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2\pi = -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

item.title: [8] Ultrafast imprinting of fused ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic skyrmions
item.description:
Last authors: Vincent Baltz, Richard F. L. Evans

Authors: Coline Thevenard, Carenza E. Cronshaw, Romain Tahay, Daria Gusakova, Vincent Baltz, Richard F. L. Evans

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental demonstration of ultrafast skyrmion imprinting in magnetic bilayers with topological relevance.

Tags: #antiferromagnetism #ferromagnetism #skyrmions #topological #ultrafast #experimental

Abstract: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are promising topologically protected entities for robust storage and THz transport of information. Their generation has so far relied on slow techniques or on specific magnetic structures, which limit their integration into spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate the imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions within a few picoseconds in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer with a thermal laser pulse. We identify a threshold energy required to initiate the fused skyrmion phase and show that this can be modulated by a magnetic field, enabling deterministic nucleation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions. Compared to conventional slow field-cooling processes to control antiferromagnets we show that laser-induced skyrmion imprinting can be orders of magnitude faster and provides an experimentally feasible route towards ultrafast creation and manipulation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions.

item.title: [7] Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe2 encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
item.description:
Last authors: Andres Castellanos-Gomez, Carlos Ant\'on-Solanas

Authors: Christos Paspalides, Brendan C. Mulkerin, Rafael Luque Merino, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant experimental study on doping and excitonic response in 2D TMD monolayers.

Tags: #experiment #MoSe2 #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. Whereas the reference is dominated by the neutral exciton, the nitride-encapsulated monolayer shows attractive and repulsive polaron resonances separated by ${\sim}31$~meV, with emission dominated by the attractive branch. A quantitative comparison of temperature-dependent reflectance with a microscopic finite-temperature Fermi-polaron theory shows that the nitride induces substantial electron doping in the monolayer, with an electron density of $(0.8$--$0.9)\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. Using the extracted density and trion binding energy as the only input parameters, the theory reproduces the photoluminescence spectra up to ${\sim}80$ K in excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, thus corroborating the Fermi-polaron description of the observed excitonic response.

item.title: [7] Coexisting orders and dipolar Luttinger liquids in ZN quantum torus chain
item.description:
Last authors: Hyun-Yong Lee, Jung Hoon Han

Authors: Seunghun Lee, Seungho Lee, Hyun-Yong Lee, Jung Hoon Han

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of Luttinger liquids and coexisting orders in 1D chains.

Tags: #theory #Luttingerliquid #1Dphysics

Abstract: We establish a unified ground-state phase diagram for the one-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ quantum torus chain, which is connected to dipolar cluster and dipolar Ising chains via noninvertible dualities. Combining tensor-network calculations with bosonization and perturbation theory, we establish a rich phase diagram governed by the local Hilbert-space dimension $N$ and its parity. We identify phases with coexisting $X$ and $Z$ long-range orders ($C$ phase), and dipolar Luttinger liquids (dLL$_{\rm I}$ and dLL$_{\rm II}$) separating coexisting phases from single-order phases. Gapless dipolar excitations coexist with long-range order in dLLs. Both the $C$ and dLL phases appear at $N \geq 5$, but only the $C$ phases persist as $N\to \infty$. The stability of the dLL phase is understood by an emergent Luttinger liquid theory, with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions out of it driven by competing umklapp and clock anisotropy perturbations. For odd $N \geq 5$, a third dLL phase (dLL$_{\rm III}$) emerges near $\theta = \pi$ due to the low-energy dynamics inside the exponentially degenerate ground-state manifold that maps onto an effective XXZ chain. Duality considerations suggest a possible gapless dipolar symmetry-protected topological phase and spontaneous dipole-symmetry breaking in dipolar cluster chains.

item.title: [7] Reconfigurable 2D Lateral Heterostructure Platform for Unified Detection, Emission, and Logic
item.description:
Last authors: Mayank Shrivastava, Prasana Kumar Sahoo

Authors: Purbasha Ray, Rupali Verma, Biswajeet Nayak, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental multifunctional device based on MoSe2-WSe2 lateral heterostructures.

Tags: #experiment #heterostructure #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Heterogeneous integration of sensing, light generation, communication, and computation typically requires specialized devices, resulting in complex interconnects, fabrication overhead, parasitic losses, and energy penalties. Developing a monolithic, reconfigurable device capable of controlling carrier generation, transport, and recombination remains a longstanding challenge. Two-dimensional (2D) lateral heterostructures offer a promising approach by combining spatially distinct domains of different charge polarity with a dynamically tunable electrostatic landscape. Here, multifunctional bilayer MoSe2-WSe2 lateral heterojunctions are demonstrated, integrating photodetection, reconfigurable electroluminescence (EL), and CMOS logic operation within a unified platform. The photodetector exhibits a responsivity of 35 A W-1, a specific detectivity of 5 x 10^13 Jones, and a noise-equivalent power of 6.3 x 10^-18 W Hz^-1/2, enabled by efficient charge separation and photoconductive gain. Under electrical injection, electrostatic gating dynamically switches the radiative recombination zone among the MoSe2 domain, lateral heterointerface, and WSe2 domain, enabling spatially programmable EL, optical multiplexing, and ternary optical logic. Furthermore, the complementary transport characteristics of the two domains enable CMOS inverter operation at 0.25 kHz. These functionalities originate from a common electrostatic framework in which the gate-tunable depletion region governs carrier extraction, recombination, and transport. This work establishes 2D lateral heterostructures as multifunctional building blocks for monolithically integrated electronic and optoelectronic systems combining light sensing, generation, and information processing.

item.title: [8] Intrinsic second-order nonlinear Hall effect from perturbation theory (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Hai-Zhou Lu, X. C. Xie

Authors: Zhi-Hao Wei, Xiao-Bin Qiang, Renjie Tong, Hai-Zhou Lu, X. C. Xie

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Establishes theory for intrinsic nonlinear Hall effect related to quantum geometry and Berry curvature.

Tags: #theory #Halleffect #quantumgeometry

Abstract: Nonlinear transport provides an efficient probe of the electronic structure and symmetry of quantum materials. As a prominent example, the intrinsic nonlinear Hall effect has attracted considerable attention in recent years because it is independent of impurity scattering and directly reflects the quantum geometry of Bloch electrons. Here we establish a simple textbook-style perturbation theory for the intrinsic nonlinear conductivity. Based on the well-defined Bloch-state velocity, our formulation perturbatively determines the field-corrected velocity and distribution function, from which the conductivity follows directly. We further compare our approach with wavepacket-based theories and discuss their consistency.

item.title: [7] Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Haiming Dong, Kai Chang

Authors: Xingdi Wang, Haiming Dong, Kai Chang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Quantum theory of optomagnetism in graphene's Dirac fermions via interband coherence.

Tags: #theory #graphene #Diracmatter

Abstract: The inverse Faraday effect converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into a quasistatic magnetization, providing a fundamental route to ultrafast optical control of magnetic fields. We develop an analytical quantum theory of this effect in intrinsic graphene, where massless Dirac fermions, electron-hole symmetry, and weak spin-orbit coupling suppress conventional population-based interpretations. We show that in intrinsic graphene, the helicity-dependent orbital magnetization arises from the off-diagonal zero-harmonic component of the second-order density matrix, rather than from intraband carrier circulation or diagonal population imbalance. We obtain closed expressions for the induced temporal surface magnetization, its finite-pulse dynamics, and the nonlocal stray magnetic field generated by the two-dimensional (2D) source. Optical helicity, frequency, pulse envelope, and beam profile independently control the response. Our results identify intrinsic graphene as an ideal platform for coherent orbital optomagnetism in 2D Dirac matter.

item.title: [7] Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
item.description:
Last authors: E. X. M. Trewick, M. M{\aa}nsson

Authors: D. W. Tam, {\O}. S. Fjellv{\aa}g, B. Gonano, E. X. M. Trewick, M. M{\aa}nsson

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure study of SmN exploring orbital differentiation and possible unconventional superconductivity.

Tags: #electronicstructure #superconductivity #rareearth

Abstract: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

item.title: [7] Preformed excitons in the excitonic density-wave state of monolayer 1T'-MoTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Xiaoxiang Xi, Junwei Liu

Authors: Fei Yang, Keyu Wei, Dekun Yang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of excitonic density-wave physics in a 2D material relevant to electronic structure interests.

Tags: #monolayer #electronic-structure #density-wave

Abstract: Phase-incoherent preformed excitons have long been anticipated in excitonic insulators, yet their characteristic signatures and underlying physics remain elusive, as the electrical neutrality of excitons hinders direct probes of condensate phase coherence. Here we exploit the emergent excitonic density wave driven by phase-coherent pairings in systems hosting momentum-separated electron and hole Fermi pockets, such as monolayer 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$, as an experimentally accessible probe of excitonic phase coherence. We observe in 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$ that the density-wave order and its associated emergent collective excitations, as revealed by Raman spectroscopy, vanish above $T_c\approx80~$K, whereas the excitonic-insulator state, characterized by a single-particle gap in transport and tunneling measurements, persists up to $T_g\approx100~$K, revealing an intermediate pseudogap-like regime of preformed excitons without long-range phase coherence. Theoretically, we attribute this intriguing separation to two distinct processes governing the loss of excitonic order by its own emergent excitations: boson-driven phase decoherence and fermion-driven pair breaking. Specifically, we identify an emergent low-lying collective excitation as a lattice-pinned phason (phase mode), whose heating-induced gap softening enhances phase fluctuations and drives condensate phase decoherence above $T_c$, while thermal excitations of fermionic quasiparticles gradually suppress and ultimately destroy pairing amplitude at the higher $T_g$. The self-consistent microscopic calculation quantitatively captures our key observations, establishing an excitonic realization of preformed-pairing physics.

item.title: [7] Domain walls of a spin-chirality ferroelectric as tunable quantum particles
item.description:
Last authors: Atharva Hingane, Sergey Artyukhin

Authors: Aleksandr Buzdakov, Atharva Hingane, Sergey Artyukhin

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to frustration, chirality, and topological domain wall physics in low-dimensional spin systems.

Tags: #topological #frustration #spin-chains

Abstract: In frustrated spin chains with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange, the vector spin chirality sets the electric polarization, so a ferroelectric domain wall is a domain wall of the chirality. The semiclassical picture suggests nonlocal switching dynamics due to topological constraints on the spins, but little is known about such domain walls in a quantum spin chain. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations for a frustrated spin-1/2 XXZ chain in which a bond alternation $\delta$ opens a spin gap, we show that the wall then becomes a quantum particle. In a finite chain, it has the energy levels and wave functions of a particle in a box, and it moves under an electric field as a particle under a constant force does. In the infinite chain, its mass grows by more than two orders of magnitude as $\delta$ decreases and diverges at $\delta^*\approx0.012$, where the bottom of its band becomes flat; below $\delta^*$ the band has two degenerate minima away from its center. The large mass results from a near cancellation of in-plane and out-of-plane exchange energies.

item.title: [9] Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
item.description:
Last authors: Robert Peters, Koki Shinada

Authors: Jun \=Oik\'{e}, Robert Peters, Koki Shinada

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Very relevant to current interests in altermagnetism and magnetic topological materials.

Tags: #altermagnetism #magnetic-topological #magneto-optical

Abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $\mu$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. item.title: [8] Interfacial electrostatics: From polar insulators to charged-layer metals
item.description:
Last authors: Philippe Ghosez, Nicola A. Spaldin

Authors: Edith Simmen, Nicholas C. Bristowe, Philippe Ghosez, Nicola A. Spaldin

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to oxide interface physics, electronic structure, and rare-earth nickelates.

Tags: #nickelate #electronic-structure #interfaces

Abstract: Polar discontinuities are typically described as arising from charged atomic planes, a spontaneous polarization, or a combination, in insulating films interfaced with vacuum, nonpolar insulators or metals. The resulting electrostatics are well established for systems such as LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, BaTiO$_3$/SrRuO$_3$, and BiFeO$_3$/SrRuO$_3$. However, recent observations of "polar-discontinuity-like" behavior at interfaces in which the metal contains formally charged layers (e.g., rare-earth nickelates) challenge this picture. In this work, we summarize the theoretical framework used to define and quantify interface charge, layer polarization, and screening in the three reference systems above, and then discuss signatures attributed to the formal-charge polar discontinuity arising when SmNiO$_3$, a metal with formally charged (001) layers, is interfaced with ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$. We show how concepts developed for polar discontinuities between two insulators and for screening at metallic interfaces can rationalize the reported effects and identify where our understanding of these systems leaves open questions.

item.title: [7] Canonical spin glass behavior and memory effects in van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2
item.description:
Last authors: D. Samal, Prabhat Mandal

Authors: P. Biswal, Kakan Deb, Nitesh Kumar, D. Samal, Prabhat Mandal

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Interesting magnetism in a van der Waals material, relevant to broader quantum materials interests.

Tags: #material #magnetism #vanderWaals

Abstract: We demonstrate the canonical spin-glass behavior and non-equilibrium dynamics in a single-crystalline Ni-doped van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2 with a freezing temperature $T_f \approx 45.5$ K from detailed ac susceptibility and dc magnetization measurements. The temperature-dependent dc magnetization exhibits strong magnetic irreversibility and the ac susceptibility shows that the peak at $T_f$ shifts towards higher temperatures with increase in ac frequency, indicating the presence of a spin glass state. The relative shift of the freezing temperature $\delta T_f$ per decade of frequency in ac susceptibility is estimated to be 0.0072. Dynamic scaling analysis of the frequency-dependent freezing temperature using the power law reveals the single spin flip relaxation time $\tau_0=2\times10^{-13}$ s and critical exponent $z\nu=8.1$, while the Vogel-Fulcher law yields Vogel-Fulcher temperature $T_0=43$ K and activation energy $E_a/k_B=81$ K with $E_a/k_BT_0=1.88$. The obtained values of these characteristic parameters lie well within the range associated with a canonical spin glass. The detailed non-equilibrium dynamics study, involving the magnetic relaxation and memory effect, further confirms the glassy behavior. The memory effect in zero-field-cooled magnetization establishes that the glassy state arises from the cooperative spin-spin interaction and not from superparamagnetism. The asymmetric response of magnetic relaxation with respect to negative and positive temperature cycle favors the hierarchical model of memory effects over the droplet model.

item.title: [8] Engineering antiferromagnetic (LaVO3)m/(PrVO3)n superlattices
item.description:
Last authors: Q. M. Ramasse, O. Copie

Authors: A. Benedit-Cardenas, G. Masset, M. Bugnet, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-quality superlattice engineering and interfacial electronic structure investigation in oxides.

Tags: #material #oxide #correlated

Abstract: In this study, we demonstrate the atomic-scale engineering of antiferromagnetic (LaVO3)m/(PrVO3)n superlattices grown by MBE on (001)-oriented SrTiO3 substrates. Our work achieved a precise layer-by-layer control, revealing how interface-driven structural distortions can be systematically tuned. X-ray diffraction and reciprocal space mapping confirm both the epitaxial strain state and the high crystalline quality of the superlattices. High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy further uncovers layer-resolved atomic displacements, where La3+ and Pr3+ exhibit antipolar motions modulated by the superlattice periodicity. The alternate stackings of LaVO3 and PrVO3 yield a unique antiferromagnetic transition temperature, which can be tuned by adjusting their relative proportions. This behavior exists despite the distinct spin ordering temperatures observed in the constituent materials. Layer-resolved spectroscopic measurements reveal that the hybridization of La and Pr 5d orbitals with O 2p orbitals is also modulated and directly correlated to the oxygen octahedra rotations. By determining the orbital hybridization and mapping the cation displacements as proxies, we can visualize indirectly the trilinear coupling between oxygen octahedra rotations and antipolar rare earth displacements. Notably, the interfacial oxygen octahedra connectivity between cubic SrTiO3 substrate and orthorhombic vanadate layers significantly influences the structural distortions. These distortions, almost quenched near the interface, relax over few unit cells, demonstrating how strain and interfacial effects propagate through the superlattice. This study illustrates how artificial superlattices can be engineered to control structural distortions at the atomic scale, offering a pathway to tune the magnetic properties through strain-distortion relationships in perovskite oxides.

item.title: [8] Structural Response to the Hidden Charge Order in Sr3Fe2O7
item.description:
Last authors: Jochen Geck, Dmytro S. Inosov

Authors: Darren C. Peets, Nikita D. Andriushin, Tobias Ritschel, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct investigation of charge order and electronic phase transition in a correlated system.

Tags: #material #chargeorder #correlated

Abstract: We previously reported `hidden' charge order below $\sim$330 K in the centrosymmetric skyrmion host Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_7$ [J.-H. Kim et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 097203 (2021)], finally identifying the charge disproportionation and localization transition that had been first seen in the 1960s. We detected this through resonant x-ray scattering, which directly probes electron density, but is only indirectly sensitive to the lattice structure. This left open the question of whether the charge-ordering transition has a true structural component or consists merely of the reorganization of electrons. Neutrons probe the lattice directly, and we now show, based on neutron data, that the charge order is accompanied by a clear structural modification.

item.title: [7] Electrical addressing of compensated magnetic order in artificial spin ice
item.description:
Last authors: Ale\v{s} Hrabec, Laura J. Heyderman

Authors: St\'ephane Nilsson, Lauren J. Riddiford, Emily Darwin, Hans J. Hug, Ale\v{s} Hrabec, Laura J. Heyderman

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of compensated magnetic order and electrical control in engineered systems.

Tags: #material #magnetism #spintronics

Abstract: Compensated magnetic systems, such as antiferromagnets, hold immense potential for spintronic devices thanks to vanishing stray fields, robustness to perturbations, and ultrafast dynamics. Yet, electrical writing and reading of their order remains a major challenge. Here we use artificial spin ice as a mesoscale platform in which compensated order can be engineered, directly imaged, and electrically controlled. Specifically, we demonstrate combined electrical writing and reading of a compensated state in a triangular artificial spin ice. Exploiting the orientation dependence of the spin-orbit torque switching current, we independently switch three nanomagnet sublattices through a single current channel, with the planar Hall effect providing sublattice-resolved readout. This grants access to all eight magnetization states of the triangular plaquette, including its fully compensated state, yielding a nonlinear, history-dependent electrical response. Our results establish an approach to electrically programmable compensated magnetic systems and provide an important foundation for reconfigurable magnetic devices and unconventional computing.

item.title: [8] Ab initio Engineering of Topological Superconductivity in Substrate-Supported Magnetic Chains
item.description:
Last authors: Andr\'{a}s L\'{a}szl\'{o}ffy, Balazs Ujfalussy

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance to topological superconductivity and Majorana states in realistic heterostructure models.

Tags: #topological #superconductivity #Majorana #theory

Abstract: In this paper, we employ a combination of several first-principles-based approaches to systematically scan chains of several types of magnetic atoms in different chain geometries on top of various overlayers on the Nb(110) surface, to develop a pathway to engineer topological Majorana edge states. Using atomistic spin-model calculations, we first identify a rich variety of magnetic configurations, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, spin-spiral, and exotic up-up-down-down states stabilized solely within a second-order Heisenberg model. In the next step, we solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations using a band-theoretical method. Depending on the magnetic structure and atomic configuration, the superconducting spectra may exhibit topologically trivial minigaps, broad overlapping Shiba bands, or localized zero-energy edge states accompanied by sizable topological minigaps. In particular, Fe chains on Ag/Nb(110) are found to display pronounced signatures associated with topological superconductivity, including strongly localized zero-energy edge states and indications of Shiba band inversion. We further demonstrate that changes in the spin structure or a small amount of spatial relaxation can substantially modify the superconducting band structure and the localization properties of the edge states.

item.title: [7] Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Textures at Chiral Molecule-Metal Interfaces
item.description:
Last authors: Amos Afugu, Zhen-Fei Liu

Authors: Gyanu P. Kafle, Amos Afugu, Zhen-Fei Liu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to ARPES methodology and interpretation of spin/orbital textures in surface states.

Tags: #ARPES #spin-orbit #surfacestates

Abstract: Chiral molecular adsorption can modify the spin and orbital character of metal surface states, providing an electronic-structure basis for interpreting spin-dependent interfacial phenomena. Using first-principles calculations with spin-orbit coupling, band unfolding, and an atom-projected orbital angular momentum (OAM) analysis, we investigate spin and OAM textures at chiral heptahelicene/Au(111) interfaces and compare them with clean Au (111) and an achiral coronene/Au system. Adsorption changes the orientations of the spin and OAM vectors and reduces the sampled OAM magnitudes of Au-derived surface states near the Fermi level. The two heptahelicene enantiomers exhibit textures related by mirror and time-reversal symmetries, whereas the comparison with coronene identifies changes that also occur without molecular chirality. These results clarify how molecular adsorption modifies interfacial spin and orbital character and establish symmetry constraints relevant to chirality-dependent photoemission.

item.title: [9] Atomic-scale Imaging of Time Reversal Breaking Supercurrents in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8
item.description:
Last authors: Jonathan Ward, J. C. S\'eamus Davis

Authors: Bin Hu, Catherine Dawson, Shuqiu Wang, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: J. C. S\'eamus Davis

Tags: #cuprate #superconduct

Abstract: A persistent mystery of CuO_2-based high temperature superconductivity has been the mechanism and consequences of time reversal ($\mathcal{T}$)-symmetry breaking. Although theoretical hypotheses focus upon persistent electronic currents as a potential cause, these have been invisible to direct experimental probes. That impasse has recently been removed by development of techniques for atomic-scale supercurrent visualization. Here, by imaging the energy-resolved density of electronic states $N(r,E)$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$, we search for the specific signatures of flowing supercurrents in a disordered $d$-wave superconductor. Employing the strategy of artificial neural networks (ANN) for complex quantum matter visualization, we designed a dual-ANN (VMAP) to efficiently implement $d$-wave supercurrent visualization, achieving imaging of supercurrent speeds $V(r)$ at magnetic fields $|B| \leq \mu T$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$. Correspondence between specific characteristics of $N(r,E)$ around each supercurrent loop and a quantum "Rosetta Stone" which translates $N(r,E)$ to $V(r)$, emphasizes the validity of $V(r)$ detection and visualization. Then, for hole-densities 0.17 $\leq p \leq$ 0.22 we observe statistically repeatable networks of supercurrent flows. Crucially, these supercurrents satisfy Kirchhoff's law at junctions within each network. Further, theoretical predictions for supercurrent speeds $V$ in disordered $d$-wave superconductors are consistent with measured 1250 m/s $< V <$ 4000 m/s, and with reported magnetic field amplitudes $|B| \approx$ 0.1 mT Thus, detection and visualization of these supercurrent loop networks provides unique perspectives on $\mathcal{T}$-symmetry breaking in cuprates. It also emphasizes the accelerating utility of ANN techniques for physics discovery from high data volume quantum matter research.

item.title: [8] Charge-transfer excitation drives cooperative phonon-assisted exciton self-trapping in NiPS3
item.description:
Last authors: Peter Uhd Jepsen, Binbin Zhou

Authors: Long Cheng, Alexander Holm Ohrt, Oliver Nagy, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experiment on correlated van der Waals magnets, relevant for spectroscopic interpretation.

Tags: #vanderWaals #correlated #spectroscopy

Abstract: Carrier self-trapping is a fundamental relaxation pathway in strongly correlated quantum materials, yet the microscopic lattice motions that drive it have remained largely inaccessible to direct observation. Here we investigate the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS$_3$ upon excitation across its ligand-to-metal charge-transfer gap, and reveal a nonequilibrium pathway that initially generates unbound carriers before they evolve into correlated excitonic states. Using ultrabroadband optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, we simultaneously track carrier localization and the associated lattice dynamics in real time. The transient conductive response quenches with a time constant of $\sim$109 fs and evolves into a localized exciton state, accompanied by pronounced renormalization of Ni-S optical phonons and the emergence of a transient 2.7 THz vibrational mode. Temperature-dependent measurements, together with mode-resolved dielectric dynamics and symmetry analysis, identify the 2.7 and 8.0 THz responses as spectroscopic indicators of exciton self-trapping and point to a cooperative two-phonon mechanism. These findings establish the excitation pathway as a key parameter controlling carrier localization and many-body relaxation in strongly coupled quantum materials.

Using ultrabroadband optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, we simultaneously track carrier localization and the associated lattice dynamics in real time. The transient conductive response quenches with a time constant of $\sim$109 fs and evolves into a localized exciton state, accompanied by pronounced renormalization of Ni-S optical phonons and the emergence of a transient 2.7 THz vibrational mode. Temperature-dependent measurements, together with mode-resolved dielectric dynamics and symmetry analysis, identify the 2.7 and 8.0 THz responses as spectroscopic indicators of exciton self-trapping and point to a cooperative two-phonon mechanism. These findings establish the excitation pathway as a key parameter controlling carrier localization and many-body relaxation in strongly coupled quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality
item.description:
Last authors: Daniel Loss, Mircea Trif

Authors: Dimitrije Stepanenko, Daniel Loss, Mircea Trif

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of spin chirality and Mott insulators with potential implications for magnetic materials.

Tags: #magnetism #Mottinsulator #theory

Abstract: Gauge invariance forbids equilibrium photon condensation for spatially uniform electric-dipole coupling, motivating alternative routes based on orbital magnetic response. We show that triangular molecular magnets coupled to a cavity support photon condensation driven by emergent scalar spin chirality. Starting from the half-filled Hubbard model in the Mott regime, we derive an effective Hamiltonian in which virtual ring exchange couples the cavity flux directly to scalar spin chirality. Mean-field theory, collective-fluctuation calculations, and finite-size exact diagonalization reveal a phase with spontaneous chirality ordering and a macroscopic cavity displacement, together with hybrid chirality-photon excitations. The condensation threshold can be tuned electrically through the molecular chirality splitting. Our results establish emergent orbital degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets as a route to equilibrium light-matter ordering beyond conventional dipolar cavity quantum electrodynamics.

item.title: [8] Multiple Field-Induced Transitions, Magnetocaloric Response and Anisotropic Magnetotransport in Orthorhombic RAlGe (R = Dy, Ho)
item.description:
Last authors: D. E. Graf, J. Paglione

Authors: Ram Kumar, D. S. Sokratov, P. Sobel, C. Mueller, D. E. Graf, J. Paglione

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of RAlGe Weyl semimetals relevant to magnetic topological materials and transport.

Tags: #Weyl #transport #magnetictopologicalmaterials

Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the magnetic, thermodynamic, and magnetocaloric properties of single-crystalline DyAlGe and HoAlGe, both members of the RAlGe Weyl semimetal family. Magnetization, heat capacity and transport measurements reveal multiple magnetic phase transitions associated with the evolution of complex magnetic structures. For DyAlGe, the primary magnetic ordering occurs at \textit{$T_{N1}$}= 30.5 K , while HoAlGe orders at a much lower temperature of \textit{$T_{N1}$}= 11.5 K, followed by additional first-order magnetic transitions at 6.6 K and 8 K, respectively. The magnetization isotherms display pronounced anisotropy for the B $\parallel$ a, consistent with competing exchange and crystal-field interactions. The magnetic entropy change ($\Delta S_M$) derived from isothermal magnetization demonstrates a significant magnetocaloric effect (MCE) with sign change in both systems, with a maximum $\Delta S_M$ of $\approx$ 5$-$23 J/kg-K along B $\parallel$ a for a field change of 0$-$7 T. The sign reversal of $\Delta S_M$ across field-induced transitions highlights the complex field-tuned spin configurations. The moderate MCE and magnetic anisotropy suggest that these materials may serve as model systems for studying magnetocaloric effects in topologically nontrivial intermetallics with interplay between localized 4\textit{f} magnetism and crystal symmetry.

item.title: [8] Emergent Attraction and Competing Orders near the Van Hove Singularity in Rhombohedral n-layer Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Yang-Zhi Chou, Sankar Das Sarma

Authors: Jing-Yu Zhao, Yang-Zhi Chou, Sankar Das Sarma

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of competing CDW/PDW orders in graphene systems relevant to the reader's broader interest.

Tags: #graphene #CDW #superconductivity

Abstract: Unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral $n$-layer graphene exhibits a rich phase diagram with multiple distinct superconducting regions, whose microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we investigate the competition between charge-density-wave (CDW) and pair-density-wave (PDW) instabilities near the inner van Hove singularities (VHSs), using a patch renormalization-group approach with the realistic band structures incorporated. We identify two key findings. First, we find an effective attractive interaction emerging from purely repulsive interactions through RG flow in the presence of $C_3$ symmetry breaking. The resulting interaction structure, with two repulsive couplings and one attractive coupling, gives rise to competing CDW and PDW instabilities. Second, the competition is controlled by the detuning from the VHS. While CDW dominates near the VHS filling and at higher temperatures, PDW becomes the leading instability on either side of the VHS and at lower temperatures. This mechanism naturally produces two superconducting regions separated by a CDW-dominated regime, providing a possible qualitative explanation for the experimentally observed separation between SC1 and SC2.

item.title: [7] Evidence for crystal-field-selected octupolar order in wolframite oxides
item.description:
Last authors: Martin M\r{a}nsson, Yasmine Sassa

Authors: Ugne Miniotaite, Leonid V. Pourovskii, Ola K. Forslund, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of exotic magnetic order in oxides; interesting experimental characterization for magnetic materials.

Tags: #antiferromagnet #material

Abstract: Magnetic order can involve higher-rank moments such as octupoles, which are difficult to identify in strongly distorted crystals. Here we present evidence for predominantly octupolar order in the monoclinic wolframites MgReO$_4$ and ZnReO$_4$. Muon spin spectroscopy detects magnetic transitions near 83 and 126 K, respectively, with similar precession frequencies in both compounds. An ab initio effective Hamiltonian shows that strong crystal fields split the spin--orbit quartet, isolating low-energy doublets with weak dipolar character. Exchange selects octupole-dominated order in distinct collinear antiferromagnetic structures, with moments along $b$ in MgReO$_4$ and tilted within the $ac$ plane in ZnReO$_4$. The estimated dipole moments of 0.06 and 0.12 $\mu_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Re, respectively, are consistent with the absence of a resolved magnetic contribution in neutron powder diffraction. A single-ion model illustrates how octupolar states generate local fields with a vanishing net dipole moment. These findings support a crystal-field route to hidden magnetism beyond double perovskites.

item.title: [8] Phonon-mediated intrinsic topological superconductivity in Fermi arcs (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Masoud Bahari, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

Authors: Kristian M{\ae}land, Masoud Bahari, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of topological superconductivity on Weyl semimetal surfaces, directly relevant to the user profile.

Tags: #Weyl #Majorana #superconduct #topological

Abstract: We propose that phonons can intrinsically mediate topological superconductivity on the surface of Weyl semimetals. Weyl semimetals are gapless topological materials with nondegenerate zero energy surface states known as Fermi arcs. We derive the phonon spectrum and electron-phonon coupling in an effective model of a Weyl semimetal and apply weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory of superconductivity. In a slab geometry, we find that surface superconductivity dominates over bulk superconductivity in a range of chemical potentials around the Weyl nodes. The superconducting gap function realizes spinless chiral $p$-wave Cooper pairing in the Fermi arcs, leading to Majorana bound states in the core of vortices. Furthermore, we find a suppression of the absolute value of the gap in the center of the Fermi arcs, which is not captured by a local Hubbard attraction. The suppression is due to the nonlocal origin of electron-phonon coupling, leading to a layer dependence which has important consequences for topological surface states.

item.title: [9] Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
item.description:
Last authors: Jonathan Gaudet, Alannah M. Hallas

Authors: Ashutosh K. Singh, Niclas Heinsdorf, Abraham A. Mancilla, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Experimental neutron scattering on a metallic altermagnet, highly relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #experiment #altermagnet #neutronscattering #magnons #CrSb

Abstract: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.

item.title: [8] Fractional quantization in gapless flat bands with ill-defined topology and divergent quantum geometry
item.description:
Last authors: Dawei Zhai, Wang Yao

Authors: Wenqi Yang, Dawei Zhai, Wang Yao

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on FQAH effect in gapless flat bands, related to anomalous Hall and quantum geometry.

Tags: #theory #FQAH #anomalousHall #flatbands #quantumgeometry

Abstract: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) effect, a zero-magnetic-field lattice analog of the fractional quantum Hall effect, offers a unique pathway toward fault-tolerant quantum computation and deep insights into the interplay of topology and strong correlations. The exploration has been successfully guided by the paradigm of ideal flat Chern bands, which mimic Landau levels in both band topology and local quantum geometry. Yet, given the boundless potential for Bloch bands in lattice systems, it remains a significant open question whether FQAH states can arise in scenarios fundamentally distinct from this paradigm. Here we turn to a class of gapless flat bands, featuring (i) ill-defined band topology, (ii) non-quantized Berry flux, (iii) divergent quantum geometry at singular band touchings, (iv) highly fluctuating and far-from-ideal quantum geometry across the Brillouin zone. Our exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group calculations unambiguously demonstrate an FQAH phase that is virtually independent of the interaction strength, persisting from the weak-interaction to the strong-interaction limit. We find the stability of the FQAH states does not uniquely correlate with the singularity strength. Instead, the many-body topological order can adapt to the singular and fluctuating quantum geometric landscape by spontaneously developing an inhomogeneous carrier distribution, while its quenching is accompanied by a drop in the occupation-weighted Berry flux. Our work reveals a profound interplay between local quantum geometry and many-body correlation, and significantly expands the exploration space for the FQAH effect and correlated phenomena in general.

item.title: [7] Substrate Role in Polaron Formation on Single-layer Transition Metal Dihalides
item.description:
Last authors: Thomas Michely, Jeison Fischer

Authors: Affan Safeer, Oktay G\"ulery\"uz, Guangyao Miao, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental STM study of polarons in 2D materials, relevant to electronic structure and moire.

Tags: #experiment #STM #2Dmaterials #polarons #graphene

Abstract: Single-layer transition metal dihalides grown on conducting substrates were shown to host stable polarons. Here, we investigate small polarons in a single layer of the insulator MnBr$_2$, which was grown by molecular beam epitaxy on three different substrates: graphene on Ir(110), graphene on Ir(111), and Au(111). Polarons on these substrates can be created, converted, and moved by the STM tip when a tunneling current flows at a proper bias voltage. Four polaron species are observed in MnBr$_2$ grown on graphene Ir(110), three of which resemble the species previously observed for CoCl$_2$ on graphite, whereas MnBr$_2$ grown on the other substrates exhibits only two of these four species. Changing the substrate from graphene on Ir to Au(111) increases polaron number density by an order of magnitude. These large differences demonstrate that the choice of conducting substrate plays a decisive role in determining polaron phenomenology in substrate-supported single-layer insulators. Two unique observations are reported for polarons in MnBr$_2$ on graphene supported by Ir(110): First, mobile polarons are guided by the periodic potential originating from the super-moir\'e of MnBr$_2$ with graphene and Ir(110); second, polarons remain stable up to 300\,K.

item.title: [8] Moir\'e Engineering of Square-Lattice Hubbard Models for Copper- and Iron-Based Superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Pavel Volkov, Zhu-Xi Luo

Authors: Toshikaze Kariyado, Yusuf Wicaksono, Ashvin Vishwanath, Pavel Volkov, Zhu-Xi Luo

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on moiré engineering for Hubbard models relevant to cuprate and pnictide superconductors.

Tags: #theory #moire #superconductivity #Hubbardmodel #cuprates #pnictides

Abstract: We propose twisted $\Gamma$-valley square-lattice homobilayers, exemplified by ZnF$_2$, as a tunable reference platform to emulate square lattice Hubbard-type models relevant to high-temperature superconductors. With model parameters derived from first-principles calculations, the lowest moir\'e band realizes a single-orbital Hubbard model underlying cuprates, while the next two realize a $p_x, p_y$ model with the minimal symmetry structure of pnictide $d_{xz}$, $d_{yz}$ Hamiltonians. Hartree-Fock analysis further predicts an antiferro-orbital ferromagnetic insulator at quarter filling.

item.title: [8] A Correlated Route to Antiferromagnetic Spintronics
item.description:
Last authors: Joel Bobadilla, Alberto Camjayi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on spintronics in correlated antiferromagnets and altermagnets using Hubbard model.

Tags: #theory #altermagnet #antiferromagnet #spintronics #Hubbardmodel #DMFT #correlated

Abstract: Antiferromagnets are attractive for spintronics owing to their vanishing net magnetization and ultrafast spin dynamics, yet their spin-compensated electronic structure has long confined them to passive roles. Here we identify a symmetry selection rule that overcomes this limitation: in a collinear antiferromagnet, a spin-polarized dc charge current requires the simultaneous breaking of particle--hole symmetry and of the equivalence between the two magnetic sublattices, either one alone leaving the polarization identically zero. We demonstrate the rule in the doped antiferromagnetic Hubbard model within dynamical mean-field theory: doping and a uniform magnetic field each break one of the two symmetries, and electronic correlations convert the resulting asymmetries into a sizable, field-tunable polarization of the charge current. The polarization is largest deep in the ordered phase and reverses sign at an emergent compensation point, set by the hierarchy of spin-dependent scattering rates and not dictated by symmetry, at which the dominant conducting spin species is interchanged. In correlated altermagnetic Hubbard models, the same two symmetries are broken structurally, by the sublattice-alternating hopping pattern: the field-driven mechanism identified here and the altermagnetic one are two realizations of a single selection rule. Electronic correlations thus emerge as an active ingredient for spintronics in structurally conventional collinear antiferromagnets.

item.title: [8] Probing bilayer topological order with layer-resolved transport (Phys. Rev. Lett.)
item.description:
Last authors: J. I. A. Li, D. E. Feldman

Authors: Hongquan Liu, J. I. A. Li, D. E. Feldman

Published as: Phys. Rev. Lett. DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory proposing experimental transport probes for topological order in relevant 2D materials.

Tags: #theory #transport #topologicalorder #graphene #2Dmaterials #quantumHall

Abstract: Shot noise has been used to measure fractional charges of anyons. The value of the charge imposes constraints on fractional statistics but does not determine it. This limitation is particularly important in multi-component systems. For example, the zero charge of neutral anyons in bilayer graphene gives no information about their statistics at all. We propose a way to shed light on the statistics of charged and neutral anyons in multi-component systems with layer-resolved or spin- resolved noise. The protocol applies to the fractional quantum spin Hall effect in MoTe$_2$, topological states in multi-layer graphene and bilayer GaAs, and to recently discovered fractional excitons in bilayer graphene. The approach relies on the relation between statistics and the distribution of the anyon charge over the components. Information about statistics can also be extracted from a simpler measurement of the layer-resolved electric current through a narrow constriction in a Hall bar even in the presence of long-range interactions and other non-universal effects.

item.title: [8] Tunable Emergent Gauge Fields from Skyrmions in a Quasicrystalline Lattice (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Cristian D. Batista, Pablo S. Cornaglia

Authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Flavia A. G\'omez Albarrac\'in, Cristian D. Batista, Pablo S. Cornaglia

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of skyrmions in quasicrystalline magnets, emergent gauge fields, and tunable Hall conductivity.

Tags: #skyrmions #topological #magneticmaterials #Hall

Abstract: We study magnetic skyrmions in a two-dimensional quasicrystalline lattice using a classical Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions and an external magnetic field. The competition between the skyrmion--skyrmion repulsion and an emergent quasiperiodic pinning landscape gives rise to a sequence of distinct skyrmion lattice configurations as a function of field. The resulting hierarchy of quasiperiodic pinning potentials, characterized by closely spaced quasi-degenerate minima, enables a quasi-continuous suppression of the skyrmion density as the saturation field is approached, in sharp contrast to the strongly first-order collapse of skyrmion crystals on periodic lattices. This provides a direct mechanism for controlling the topological charge and, consequently, the emergent gauge field for itinerant electrons. As a consequence, the Hall conductivity can be strongly modified with small changes in the magnetic field and driven smoothly to zero near saturation. This field-controlled tunability, rooted in the underlying multistability, identifies quasicrystalline magnets as a platform for tunable topological textures, with potential applications in magnetic memory and magnetoelectronic response.

item.title: [9] Field-induced first order transitions and phase coexistence in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid candidate BaCo2(AsO4)2
item.description:
Last authors: Pengcheng Dai, Douglas Natelson

Authors: Tanner J. Legvold, Bin Gao, Rong-Zhu Lin, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental neutron scattering on a Kitaev spin liquid candidate, investigating magnetic transitions and excitations.

Tags: #neutronscattering #spinliquid #magneticorder #quantummaterials

Abstract: BaCo2(AsO4)2 (BCAO) is an insulating Kitaev quantum spin liquid candidate with a rich low-temperature phase diagram. Below 5 K, it exhibits double-zigzag magnetic order. Upon application of an in-plane magnetic field, the magnetic structure first transforms into an up-up-down (UUD) state near 0.12 T and then enters a fully spin-polarized ferromagnetic (FM) state near 0.5 T. In the narrow field regime close to the polarized phase, a finite residual thermal conductivity has been reported, suggesting a possible field-induced quantum spin liquid phase. Using neutron scattering, we show that the field-induced double-zigzag-to-UUD transition near 0.15 T is accompanied by the emergence of a cluster of localized UUD spin excitations that coexist with conventional spin waves. Upon further increasing field, BCAO undergoes a first-order UUD-to-FM transition with coexistence of UUD and FM phases, accompanied by a sharp response in the spin Seebeck coefficient. These results do not support a quantum spin liquid scenario near the UUD-to-FM critical field. Instead, modeling indicates that the broad excitations arise from bound spin-flip pairs, while a low-lying dispersive branch near the FM phase boundary carries the same sign of magnetization as the FM order. These excitations naturally account for the observed sign of the spin Seebeck response and are likely relevant to the thermal conductivity near the critical field.
