item.title: [8] Observation of far-from-equilibrium scaling in the transient dynamics of 2D quantum magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Jad C. Halimeh, Christian Gro{\ss}

Authors: Fabio Bensch, Umberto Borla, Federico Balducci, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of quantum magnetism on kagome and other 2D lattices using Rydberg atoms.

Tags: #quantummagnet #kagome #coldatoms #experiment #nonequilibrium

Abstract: The transient regime of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics lacks the established organizing principles that universality and scaling provide in equilibrium. It is least understood for two-dimensional short-range interacting systems, where mean-field arguments are not expected to hold, controlled theoretical descriptions are few, and fluctuations are strong. Here we investigate the quench dynamics of the transverse-field Ising model using programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realizing honeycomb, square, kagome, and triangular lattices. Starting from a fully magnetized state, we observe a pronounced softening of the dominant collective magnetization oscillation accompanied by a maximum in the damping rate, signaling a crossover between interaction- and field-dominated transient dynamics. Even though the microscopic lattice geometries are different, both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates collapse onto common curves under rescaling by the coordination-number-weighted interaction strength. We present a theoretical description which accounts for the collapse of both quantities and elucidates the nature of the processes responsible for the damping. The observed failure of the discrete truncated Wigner approximation to predict the damping for strong interactions shows that classical evolution of initial quantum noise is insufficient, while tree-tensor-network simulations reproduce the dynamics accurately. These results reveal a robust scaling regime governing the transient dynamics of short-range interacting two-dimensional quantum magnets. The fact that the dominant transient dynamics can be captured by a simple collective description despite the presence of fluctuations and nonlinearities characteristic of low dimensionality and small spin is an important insight in the quest for organizing principles in far-from-equilibrium quantum matter.

item.title: [8] Hidden Rotational Dynamics from Crystal Geometry
item.description:
Last authors: Vincent P. Flynn, Benedetta Flebus

Authors: Rule Yi, Vincent P. Flynn, Benedetta Flebus

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for phononic loop currents and TRSB from crystal geometry, highly relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #theory #crystal_symmetry #loop_current #TRSB #phonon

Abstract: From hidden spin order to electronic loop currents and frustrated fluctuations, unconventional quantum matter reveals the rich patterns that electronic and magnetic degrees of freedom form across space and time. Recent advances in chiral phononics have extended this perspective to lattice vibrations, raising the question of whether the lattice itself can generate spatially organized rotational correlations. Here we show that crystal geometry provides an autonomous mechanism for generating equilibrium angular-momentum circulation and staggered antisymmetric displacement interactions, independently of coupling to electronic or magnetic order. Our framework applies broadly to crystalline systems hosting locally symmetry-lowered environments embedded within a higher-symmetry global structure. We identify how directional elastic forces organize displacement correlations and how eliminating internal coordinates generates staggered antisymmetric interactions-a phononic analogue of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange-even in globally centrosymmetric crystals. By separating intersite angular-momentum transfer from crystalline restoring torques, we show that both elastic anisotropy and the induced antisymmetric interactions together drive oppositely circulating angular-momentum currents on neighboring plaquettes, despite vanishing mean angular momentum at every site. Sustained by quantum and thermal fluctuations, this circulation preserves time-reversal and inversion symmetry and requires neither external driving nor spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our results establish lattice geometry as a microscopic source of spatially organized angular-momentum dynamics.

item.title: [7] Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
item.description:
Last authors: P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

Authors: F. Museur, G. M. Macauley, S. Nilsson, V. Scagnoli, P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of correlated magnetism and phase transitions on an artificial kagome-related lattice, relevant for geometric insights.

Tags: #kagome #magnetism #correlated_systems #experimental

Abstract: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

item.title: [7] Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS2: from disorder through 22 and 33 order to stripe order
item.description:
Last authors: Petar Pop\v{c}evi\'c, Victor Bal\'edent

Authors: Naveen Singh Dhami, Ricardo Guillermo Torres Ramirez, Gaurav Pransu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of structural ordering in a Ni-intercalated van der Waals material (NbS2), relevant to 2D materials.

Tags: #experimental #material_synthesis #van_der_Waals #2D_materials #structural

Abstract: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

item.title: [7] High-resolution top-down nanopatterning of NbN thin films for superconducting metamaterials
item.description:
Last authors: Dmitri N. Basov, Karl K. Berggren

Authors: Francesca Incalza, Davide Mondin, Dip Joti Paul, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Methodological paper on superconducting thin films relevant for experimental device physics.

Tags: #superconduct #method #transport

Abstract: Periodic nanopatterning offers a route to tailoring vortex motion and the electromagnetic response of superconducting films, providing a basis for superconducting metamaterials. Here, we report a high-resolution top-down nanopatterning process for ultrathin epitaxial NbN films on sapphire substrates. Electron-beam lithography using hydrogen silsesquioxane (HSQ) and ZEP 530A resists was optimized through proximity-effect correction and adhesion-layer integration. Dense superconducting nanowire grids with pitches down to 70 nm were fabricated, alongside millimeter-square areas patterned with 100-nm-pitch hole arrays with high pattern fidelity. A thin Si capping layer was found to significantly improve HSQ adhesion on epitaxial NbN. The nanopatterns were successfully transferred into 5-nm-thick NbN films by reactive ion etching (RIE). Structural and dimensional characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), enabling cross-validation of nanoscale feature dimensions and etch quality. Electrical transport measurements reveal periodic resistance minima and switching-current oscillations at magnetic fields set by the hole-array pitch, consistent with enhanced vortex pinning when the vortex configuration matches the patterned lattice. Cryogenic THz time-domain spectroscopy further reveals a reduced superfluid density in the nanopatterned region relative to pristine NbN, while both regions have a spectroscopic superconducting transition near 14 K. These results establish a robust fabrication platform for superconducting nanopatterns targeting vortex pinning, metamaterials, and quantum-device applications.

item.title: [7] Topological Control of Polaritonic Flatbands in Anisotropic van der Waals Metasurfaces (Nat. Mater.)
item.description:
Last authors: Alexander A. Antonov, Andreas Tittl

Authors: Connor Heimig, Thomas Weber, Cristina Cruciano, et al.

Published as: Nat. Mater. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of topological features in anisotropic vdW materials, relevant for electronic structure/topological materials.

Tags: #experiment #vanderWaals #topological

Abstract: Anisotropic van der Waals (vdW) materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, making them valuable for tailoring directional light-matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS$_2$) stands out for its strong in-plane anisotropy and its thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons, which can hybridize with light to form exciton-polaritons. In parallel, metasurfaces, engineered arrays of nanoscale subwavelength resonators, can support ultra-sharp photonic modes in the form of quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs). Topological transformations of photonic modes can give rise to flatbands, i.e., dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Intrinsic material anisotropy offers an unexplored route to robust far-field flatband formation and control. Here, we demonstrate how structuring an intrinsically anisotropic excitonic material into a resonant metasurface fundamentally transforms its photonic topological features and light-matter coupling behavior, allowing us to drive and topologically control extended far-field flatband formation. To this end, we fabricate C$_4$-symmetric metasurfaces directly from bulk ReS$_2$. The intrinsic anisotropy lifts the initial double degeneracy of the qBIC mode and yields two distinctly polarized resonances. It also reshapes the topological landscape: the integer topological charge of the qBIC mode splits into momentum-separated half-integer singularities, thereby flattening the far-field photonic dispersion. The resulting topologically-controlled photonic flatbands are then tuned in resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS$_2$, resulting in two distinct, directionally hybridized exciton-polariton flatband regimes. These findings establish anisotropic vdW metasurfaces as a new platform for topologically engineered flatbands and flatband-driven light-matter coupling.

Here, we demonstrate how structuring an intrinsically anisotropic excitonic material into a resonant metasurface fundamentally transforms its photonic topological features and light-matter coupling behavior, allowing us to drive and topologically control extended far-field flatband formation. To this end, we fabricate C$_4$-symmetric metasurfaces directly from bulk ReS$_2$. The intrinsic anisotropy lifts the initial double degeneracy of the qBIC mode and yields two distinctly polarized resonances. It also reshapes the topological landscape: the integer topological charge of the qBIC mode splits into momentum-separated half-integer singularities, thereby flattening the far-field photonic dispersion. The resulting topologically-controlled photonic flatbands are then tuned in resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS$_2$, resulting in two distinct, directionally hybridized exciton-polariton flatband regimes. These findings establish anisotropic vdW metasurfaces as a new platform for topologically engineered flatbands and flatband-driven light-matter coupling.

item.title: [7] Cross-probing van der Waals multiferroics (Nature)
item.description:
Last authors: Hongtao Yuan, Longjiang Deng

Authors: Bo Peng, Zeya Li, Han Wang, et al.

Published as: Nature DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Review of experimental methods for 2D van der Waals multiferroics, relevant to 2D materials.

Tags: #vanderWaals #2Dmaterials #experimentalreview

Abstract: Multiferroic materials, with coupled electric and magnetic orders, hold the potential to enable low-power memory and logic devices by replacing electrical currents with electric fields for magnetic switching. Reducing the dimensionality of multiferroics, from 3D to 2D, has opened new frontiers in this already burgeoning field by enabling unprecedented control over magnetoelectric coupling that is beyond the reach of bulk counterparts, owing to reduced electrostatic screening and enhanced quantum fluctuations at the atomically thin limit. A notable example is a few-layer NiI2 multiferroic, which exhibits coexisting chiral spin textures and (anti)ferroelectricity, accompanied by strong magnetoelectric coupling; by simultaneously breaking time-reversal and spatial-inversion symmetry, NiI2 shows new physical properties such as unique mutual control of chiral magnetism and polarization with giant magnetoelectric coupling, ultrafast electromagnon excitations and odd-parity p-wave magnetism. However, there are experimental challenges in unambiguously identifying intrinsic multiferroicity. This Review critically examines the current landscape of 2D multiferroic materials, with an emphasis on experimental methodologies rather than material taxonomy. We assess different conventional probes for magnetism and ferroelectricity and identify key limitations in single-technique approaches. We emphasize the importance of magneto-opto-electric cross-correlative measurements in establishing intrinsic multiferroic behaviour and outline future research directions for both fundamental studies and device applications.

item.title: [8] Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
item.description:
Last authors: Antonio Manesco, Karsten Flensberg

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects Josephson networks to Kagome XY antiferromagnet; relevant to kagome lattice and superconductivity.

Tags: #theory #kagome #superconductivity #Josephsonjunctions

Abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-orbit coupling they also lead to spin correlations and entanglement between the trapped fermions. Our results establish fermion-induced frustration as a route to composite superconducting coherence and phase-mediated spin entanglement in superconductor-semiconductor artificial quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Towards Defect Engineering of Orbital Magnetoelectric Effects
item.description:
Last authors: Jo\~ao M. Viana Parente Lopes, Aires Ferreira

Authors: Jo\~ao M. Alendouro Pinho, Henrique P. Veiga, Alessandro Veneri, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of defect engineering for orbital magnetoelectric effects, directly related to TRSB.

Tags: #theory #orbitalmagnetism #TRSB #defects

Abstract: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental measure of time-reversal symmetry breaking in solids that is accessible by experiments. However, unlike the well-studied equilibrium case, the understanding of orbital magnetism resulting from external stimuli such as light and electric fields is still in its infancy. Here we employ a novel real-space framework to investigate charge-to-orbital conversion in a metallic orbital antiferromagnet beyond the conventional Bloch-band picture. We find that common point defects give rise to strongly enhanced time-odd magnetoelectric effects and, depending on their local symmetry, further activate otherwise-forbidden time-even responses. Moreover, we introduce a local marker that provides spatially resolved information on the orbital magnetization carried by non-equilibrium states. Real-space maps reveal that point defects create nanoscale hotspots of orbital magnetization leading to a profound modification of the bulk magnetoelectric response, including a sign reversal of the net orbital moment. Our findings may open up the possibility of engineering linear-response orbital moments with atomic-scale precision by point defects and impurities.

item.title: [7] Efficient interlayer interactions in non-planar molecule/transition-metal dichalcogenide two-dimensional heterostructure
item.description:
Last authors: Michael Shatruk, Xiao-Xiao Zhang

Authors: Johann Alvarez, Kamal Harrison, John Koptur-Palenchar, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of interlayer interactions in 2D heterostructures using monolayer TMDs.

Tags: #experiment #2Dmaterials #heterostructure #opticalspectroscopy

Abstract: Integration of molecules and two-dimensional (2D) atomic materials offer new opportunities for hybrid electronic devices. Most progress has focused on interfacing planar molecule. In contrast, incorporating non-planar molecules into 2D heterostructures remains challenging due to the three-dimensional orientations of ligands. Here we investigate interlayer interactions between discrete non-planar spin-crossover (SCO) molecules, [Fe(tBu2qsal)2] (FTBQS), monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacers through optical spectroscopies. FTBQS features bulk molecular crystal layers and can be mechanically exfoliated, enabling deterministic assembly of clean hybrid heterostructures. Robust photoluminescence (PL) quenching, even with an hBN spacer, indicates efficient F\"orster resonance energy transfer with a long decay distance. Gate-dependent optical spectroscopy further identifies charge transfer from the doping shifts in the TMD layers due to the TMD/FTBQS electronic band alignment. Our results establish efficient interlayer interactions between non-plana, discrete molecules and 2D crystals for hybrid electrical, optical, and spintronic devices.

item.title: [8] Synthesis-route-dependent state selection in the frustrated spinel ZnV2O4
item.description:
Last authors: J. Ross Stewart, Lucy Clark

Authors: Jem Pitcairn, Jennifer N. Graham, Jacob L. Brownlee, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of strongly correlated frustrated spinel using neutron scattering, showing synthesis-dependent states.

Tags: #experiment #correlatedmaterials #magnetism #neutronscattering #spinliquid

Abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

item.title: [9] Layer-dependent s superconducting pairing and influence of incipient bands in La3Ni2O7 thin films on real LaSrAlO4 substrate
item.description:
Last authors: Thomas A. Maier, Elbio Dagotto

Authors: Yang Zhang, Philip M. Dee, Ling-Fang Lin, Adriana Moreo, Thomas A. Maier, Elbio Dagotto

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of electronic structure and $s^{\pm}$ pairing in La3Ni2O7 nickelate superconducting thin films.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #theory #nickelates #superconductivity #electronicstructure #thinfilms

Abstract: Motivated by recent advances in ambient-pressure superconducting La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ (LNO) thin films, we theoretically investigate these films by explicitly incorporating the realistic LaSrAlO$_4$ (LSAO) substrate. The Fermi-surface topology of the nickelate thin film closely resembles that of the high-pressure bulk phase, with similar $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets and a small hole-like $\gamma$ pocket originating from the surface bilayer (BL3). The bonding $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ state of the interfacial bilayer (BL1, adjacent to the LSAO substrate) lies only $\sim 5$ meV below the Fermi level, giving rise to an incipient $\gamma$ band, while for the middle bilayer (BL2) its energy is much lower ($\sim 95$ meV). Remarkably, no significant spontaneous charge transfer from the LSAO substrate to the LNO film is found. Instead, {\it symmetry-allowed charge disproportionation} occurs between the BLs, with hole doping in BL3 and electron doping in BL1 and BL2. Via the weak-coupling Random Phase Approximation, we find a strong $s^{\pm}$-wave superconducting pairing instability in BL3, while $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $s^{\pm}$ are nearly degenerate in the other bilayers BL1 and BL2. Including the incipient $\gamma$ band via the Dynamical Cluster Approximation beyond weak coupling, robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing is observed in all three layers

item.title: [9] Two-Dimensional Ferromagnetic Weyl Half-Semimetal
item.description:
Last authors: Xin-Yi Chen, Lun Xiong

Authors: Yu-Yang Zhao, Chen-Hao Lv, Qing-Bo Liu, Wen-Neng Zhao, Xin-Yi Chen, Lun Xiong

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Predicts 2D ferromagnetic Weyl half-semimetal with Fermi-arc edge states, highly relevant for ARPES.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #DFT #Weyl #topological #ferromagnetism #2Dmaterials #electronicstructure

Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic topological materials provide appealing platforms for realizing spin-polarized topological states, yet the coexistence of Weyl fermions and robust high-temperature ferromagnetism remains elusive. Here, based on first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we predict monolayer BaMn$_4$O$_8$ to be a dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable ferromagnetic Weyl half-semimetal. \textcolor{blue}{An anisotropic Monte Carlo simulation on a $20\times20\times1$ lattice yields a finite-size transition estimate of approximately 1446~K.} The spin-resolved electronic structure reveals a fully spin-polarized state, in which the spin-up channel hosts linear Weyl band crossings near the Fermi level, whereas the spin-down channel remains insulating. Corresponding Fermi-arc edge states connecting the projected Weyl points (WPs) are clearly observed along the (100) boundary, confirming the nontrivial topology. Importantly, both the Weyl points and their associated Fermi arcs remain robust in the presence of spin--orbit coupling (SOC). \textcolor{blue}{These results identify monolayer BaMn$_4$O$_8$ as a candidate for fully spin-polarized topological transport.

item.title: [10] Interface Weyl electrons in the kagome-bilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Yukitoshi Motome, Atsushi Tsukazaki

Authors: Keiki Ishida, Kohei Fujiwara, Shun Sasano, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Daisuke Shiga

Tags: #kagome #Weyl #Dirac #anomalousHall #topological #transport #bandstructure

Abstract: What makes a topological character prominent is whether its characteristic electronic states are located near the Fermi energy. While the kagome-metals possess unique topological characteristics owing to their distinctive electronic band structures, i.e. flat and Dirac bands, the control of Fermi energy to accentuate these characteristics has scarcely been studied in these materials. Here, we propose a new concept for activating the topological characteristics of Weyl electrons specifically near the interface of kagome-bilayers, namely interface Weyl electrons. The kagome-bilayers prepared by a sputtering technique surprisingly exhibit atomically abrupt interfaces thanks to the suppression of interdiffusion for maintaining the crystal symmetry of the hexagonal-type D0$_{19}$ and cubic-type L1$_{2}$ structures. Much higher electrical conductivity of the kagome-bilayers compared to single-layer films indicates the emergent contribution of a highly conductive electronic state at the interfaces. The enhanced electrical conductivity and the exceptionally large anomalous Hall conductivity about 2000 $\Omega$$^{-1}$cm$^{-1}$ in the intrinsic mechanism indicates that the emergent interface electronic states comprise Weyl nodes in the D0$_{19}$ structure identified in our theoretical band calculations, triggered by nontrivial charge transfer. These results demonstrate that topological transport can be engineered at the interface of intermetallic compounds, leading further design principles towards development of device functionality.

item.title: [7] Implementation of LDA+Gutzwiller with Newton's method (Chin. Phys. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Yuan-Feng Xu, Xi Dai

Authors: Jian Zhang, Ming-Feng Tian, Guang-Xi Jin, Yuan-Feng Xu, Xi Dai

Published as: Chin. Phys. B DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Improved computational method (LDA+Gutzwiller) for electronic structure of correlated materials.

Tags: #DFT+DMFT #correlatedelectrons #electronicstructure #methodology

Abstract: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. The self-consistence process, efficiency and convergence of calculation are improved dramatically by using Newton's method with golden section search and other improvement approaches. We compare the calculated results by applying the previous linear mix method and Newton's method. We have applied our code to study the electronic structure of several typical strong correlated materials, including SrVO$_3$, LaCoO$_3$, and La$_2$O$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_2$. Our results fit quite well with the previous studies.

item.title: [7] Molecular Kondo Ball Based on an Endohedral Fullerene
item.description:
Last authors: Bing Wang, Jinlong Yang

Authors: Xiangyang Li, Xiao Zheng, Bing Wang, Jinlong Yang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical prediction of Kondo effect in a specific molecular system, relevant to correlated electrons.

Tags: #Kondoeffect #correlatedelectrons #DFT #molecularsystems

Abstract: We theoretically predict a molecular Kondo ball in TiSc$_2$N@C$_{80}$/Al(111), where a Ti-centered $S = 1/2$ local moment is encapsulated within a closed fullerene $\pi$ cage that serves as an itinerant-like electronic reservoir for Kondo screening. First-principles calculations show that intermediate molecule--substrate hybridization broadens the discrete C$_{80}$ molecular levels into itinerant-like electronic states while preserving the Ti local moment, with similar electronic conditions found for Cd(0001) and In(101).Hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) simulations reveal a temperature-dependent Fano resonance with a Kondo temperature of about 60 K.The key electronic characteristics underlying the Kondo state remain robust against adsorption orientation, demonstrating that the closed cage geometry provides an orientation-tolerant molecular architecture for Kondo screening.

First-principles calculations show that intermediate molecule--substrate hybridization broadens the discrete C$_{80}$ molecular levels into itinerant-like electronic states while preserving the Ti local moment, with similar electronic conditions found for Cd(0001) and In(101).Hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) simulations reveal a temperature-dependent Fano resonance with a Kondo temperature of about 60 K.The key electronic characteristics underlying the Kondo state remain robust against adsorption orientation, demonstrating that the closed cage geometry provides an orientation-tolerant molecular architecture for Kondo screening.

item.title: [10] Light-Induced Odd-Parity h-Wave Magnetism in Penrose Quasicrystals
item.description:
Last authors: Yiming Li, Huaqing Huang

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Predicts light-induced magnetism in quasicrystals, directly proposing spin-resolved tr-ARPES for detection.

Tags: #Floquetengineering #ARPES #magnetism #quasicrystals #theory #antiferromagnet

Abstract: Noncrystallographic rotational symmetry offers a route to unconventional spin splitting beyond the constraints of periodic crystals. We show that circularly polarized light induces odd-parity $h$-wave magnetism in a collinear antiferromagnetic Penrose quasicrystal without spin-orbit coupling. Light-induced chiral hopping, generated by virtual two-step processes, combines with staggered exchange to lift the spin degeneracy of the undriven system. Quasicrystalline spin-group symmetry enforces odd-parity spin splitting and selects $h$-wave as its leading angular harmonic. An analytical effective quasi-band theory relates this splitting to the geometry of local hopping paths and predicts its reversal upon switching the light helicity. Momentum-resolved spectral calculations reveal the characteristic alternating spin contrast, for which we propose spin-resolved time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy as an experimental probe. Our results establish a mechanism for optically controlling higher-harmonic odd-parity magnetism and demonstrate how quasicrystalline order extends Floquet engineering beyond crystallographic symmetry constraints.

item.title: [8] Two-Color Coherent Control of the Spin Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Crystals
item.description:
Last authors: Pan Zhou, Lizhong Sun

Authors: Songmin Liu, Pan Zhou, Lizhong Sun

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory paper on spin transport in altermagnets and 2D materials, directly relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #spintransport #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Spatial inversion forbids the conventional electric-dipole second-order bulk charge and spin photovoltaic responses in centrosymmetric crystals. Here we show that a phase-coherent two-color field at frequencies $\omega$ and $2\omega$ can generate symmetry-selected charge and spin photocurrents through an inversion-even third-order dc response. More importantly, the polarization direction and relative phase of the two-color field provide direct control over the current direction and can isolate transport channels in which the charge current vanishes while a finite spin current remains. A systematic symmetry analysis of centrosymmetric magnetic point groups and collinear antiferromagnetic spin point groups shows that pure-spin channels are allowed in a broad class of such systems under appropriate two-color driving. Furthermore, the relative optical phase governs both the magnitude and sign of the response. Our calculations on inversion-stacked bilayer 2H-MoS$_2$ and a centrosymmetric collinear altermagnet demonstrate resonantly enhanced, phase-tunable spin photocurrents in these complementary systems with strong and weak spin-orbit coupling, respectively. Our results establish the polarization direction and phase of coherent two-color light as active control parameters for spin transport in centrosymmetric materials.

item.title: [7] Observation of room-temperature intrinsic antiferroelectricity in van der Waals NbOCl2
item.description:
Last authors: Changsen Sun, Dawei Li

Authors: JinKai Huo, Xingyu Chen, Gaolei Zhao, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental observation of antiferroelectricity in a van der Waals material.

Tags: #experimental #2Dmaterials #vanderWaals #ferroelectricity

Abstract: In recent years, two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectricity has been extensively investigated across a wide range of 2D materials, while intrinsic 2D antiferroelectricity remains exceptionally rare, limiting its implementation in next-generation photonic and electronic devices. Here, we report the observation of room-temperature-stable antiferroelectricity in the layered transition metal oxyhalide NbOCl2, and demonstrate a reversible, stimuli-driven antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric (AFE-to-FE) phase transition in this material. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) mapping reveals a well-defined stripe-like spatial distribution of SHG intensity across as-grown NbOCl2 flakes spanning thickness from few-layer to bulk-like configurations. This distinctive SHG signature originates from the existence of antiferroelectric phase and the coexistence of antiferroelectric and ferroelectric phases within individual crystals, as evidenced by a combined incident-angle-dependent SHG measurement and Raman spectroscopy. By integrating NbOCl2 with one-dimensional silver nanowires, we achieve spatially selective, strain-mediated AFE-to-FE phase transition. Moreover, an ultralow electric field (~20 kV/cm) induces a reversible SHG response, consistent with switching from the centrosymmetric antiferroelectric state (SHG-silent) to the non-centrosymmetric ferroelectric state (SHG-active). This study not only expands the family of room-temperature 2D antiferroelectrics but also establishes a versatile platform for dynamic manipulation of nonlinear light, paving the way toward electric-field-programmable nonlinear photonics and optical information processing.

item.title: [7] Non-Abelian Hall Effects of Flavor-Waves in CP2 Skyrmions
item.description:
Last authors: Alvaro S. Nunez, Roberto E. Troncoso

Authors: Carlos Saji, Eduardo Saavedra, Alvaro S. Nunez, Roberto E. Troncoso

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of non-Abelian Hall effects and topological bands in 2D magnetic skyrmion systems.

Tags: #theory #topological #Halleffect #magnetism #skyrmions

Abstract: We investigate the collective excitations of isolated and crystalline $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ skyrmions in a two-dimensional triangular-lattice spin-1 magnet. Within an $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ coherent-state framework, fluctuations of the magnetic dipole and quadrupole moments are described by two coupled bosonic flavors. In a uniform spin-polarized state, these flavors can be identified with single-spin-flip and double-spin-flip excitations, whereas a nonuniform $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ texture mixes their character. We formulate the corresponding bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes problem and examine the matrix-valued gauge connection governing flavor-wave propagation. For isolated skyrmions, the calculated spectrum contains localized modes, and the scattering dynamics exhibit transverse deflection accompanied by isospin precession. For a numerically relaxed skyrmion crystal, we obtain collective-mode bands with nonzero Chern numbers and calculate the associated thermal Hall response. These findings illustrate how projective magnetic textures couple multipolar excitations to non-Abelian transport and topological band phenomena.

item.title: [7] Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-s Band or A-Pocket
item.description:
Last authors: Karsten Held, Liang Si

Authors: Ao Zhang, Chao Deng, Leonard M. Verhoff, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT+DMFT study of unconventional nickelate superconductors, relevant for electronic structure.

Tags: #nickelate #superconductivity #DFT+DMFT #electronicstructure

Abstract: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

item.title: [8] Spin dynamics in disordered systems with generic spin-momentum couplings: A matrix-rational formulation
item.description:
Last authors: Masataka Kakoi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for spin dynamics in altermagnets and Weyl semimetals, highly relevant to user interests.

Tags: #theory #spindynamics #altermagnetism #Weylsemimetal

Abstract: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings. Starting from the Diffuson, we introduce a matrix-valued rational approximation for its frequency dependence that does not rely on a low-frequency or weak-coupling expansion. The resulting pole equation is recast as a quadratic eigenvalue problem, from which the real-time evolution of the disorder-averaged density matrix is constructed. We apply the formulation to a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba and linear and cubic Dresselhaus couplings, a $d$-wave altermagnet with Rashba coupling, and a three-dimensional double-Weyl model. Comparisons with direct numerical simulations demonstrate quantitative agreement for both the post-quench spin dynamics and spin relaxation times across a broad range of coupling strengths, extending beyond the diffusive regime. The matrix-rational formulation provides a unified description of ultrafast spin dynamics and long-time relaxation.

item.title: [9] Hidden topological signatures in a van der Waals ferromagnet revealed by spin-resolved circular-dichroic photoemission
item.description:
Last authors: James G. Analytis, Alexander X. Gray

Authors: Jay R. Paudel, Federico Mazzola, Lidia A. Lapinski, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: photoemission

Tags: #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #Berrycurvature #vanderWaals #superconduct #correlated #topological #ferromagnet

Abstract: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Waals ferromagnet with a transition temperature of 58 K that lies close in composition to a superconducting phase that emerges upon Ni depletion. Here, we combine spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, circular-dichroism measurements, and density functional theory calculations to investigate its spin-resolved electronic structure. We observe spin-polarized states crossing the Fermi level and signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry in the ferromagnetic state. Spin-resolved circular-dichroism measurements further reveal a helicity-dependent spin response consistent with a finite spin Berry curvature and suggestive of local topological character. Together, these results establish an experimental connection between ferromagnetism, spin-polarized electronic states, and topological signatures in $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$, providing a foundation for investigating how these properties may relate to the emergence of superconductivity upon Ni depletion.

item.title: [7] Unified Theory for Momentum-Space Nonsymmorphic Symmetry of Spin Space Groups
item.description:
Last authors: Zheng Zhang, Y. X. Zhao

Authors: Peiyuan Wang, Zheng Zhang, Y. X. Zhao

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Fundamental theory of momentum-space symmetry for spin space groups, relevant for electronic band structure and topology.

Tags: #theory #symmetry #electronicstructure #topologicalmaterials

Abstract: Projective crystal symmetry provides a route to nonsymmorphic symmetry structures in momentum space, but a general theory for their realization in spin space groups has been lacking. We show that a nonsymmorphic momentum-space action is possible only when the unitary translation subgroup is combined with rotations about a common axis for a coplanar or noncoplanar spin space group of spin-$1/2$ systems. Its factor system originates entirely from the double cover $\mathrm{Spin}(2)\to SO(2)$, yielding a general formula for the fractional reciprocal-lattice translations and hence for the point-group action on the Brillouin zone. We further prove that a momentum-space nonsymmorphic group is realizable by a spin space group if and only if its Brillouin-zone action contains a two-point orbit. Consequently, 842 of the 1,357 nonsymmorphic magnetic space groups are realizable by spin space groups. Applying this theory, we construct a database covering all 67,475 SSGs that can be queried bidirectionally: from an SSG to its momentum-space magnetic group, or from a given momentum-space magnetic group to all SSGs that realize it. Together, these results establish the momentum-space symmetry foundation for a systematic band theory of SSGs in spin-$1/2$ systems.

item.title: [9] Finite-temperature effects on the single-particle Green's function of a mobile impurity in a Luttinger liquid
item.description:
Last authors: Lorenzo Gotta, Thierry Giamarchi

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: Luttinger liquid

Tags: #Luttinger #phonon

Abstract: We consider the problem of a quadratically-dispersing quantum impurity interacting through a contact density-density term with a one-dimensional (1D) superfluid described by Luttinger liquid theory. By means of a field-theoretical approach based on the linked-cluster expansion, we quantitatively address the effects of a finite temperature of the 1D bath on the momentum-space single-particle Green's function. Through a careful identification of the resonant phonon-impurity scattering processes, we obtain asymptotic large-time estimates for the thermally-induced exponential damping of the zero-temperature signal both in the $\textit{quasiparticle}$ regime, dominated by the presence of a finite lifetime for the host impurity, and in the $\textit{infrared-dominated}$ regime, where the impurity causes a Anderson's orthogonality catastrophe of the 1D bath. In both cases, we identify a temperature-induced coherence time that sets the characteristic timescale of the exponentially-decaying finite-temperature correction to the amplitude of the zero-temperature single-particle Green's function. Moreover, we draw connections between the aforesaid thermal timescale and the microscopic parameters of the Lieb-Liniger model, which admits an effective Luttinger-liquid description, highlighting the dependence of the inverse coherence time on the intra-bath interactions across the different dynamical regimes of the impurity.

item.title: [7] Atomic-scale assembly of sulfur vacancy complexes for tailored in-gap states in monolayer WS2
item.description:
Last authors: Hannu-Pekka Komsa, Wouter Jolie

Authors: Daniel Jansen, Guangyao Miao, Jan-Heinrich Keienburg, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STM/STS study of engineered electronic states in 2D monolayer semiconductor.

Tags: #STM/STS #2Dmaterials #electronicstructure #defects

Abstract: Atomic-scale defects in two-dimensional semiconductors are quasi-isolated quantum systems with promise for emerging technologies. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. In this work we assemble sulfur vacancies in monolayer WS$_{2}$ into complexes of different sizes and geometries using the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states. Among the realized sulfur vacancy complexes, we characterize two configurations that are candidates for bright single photon emitters. Our findings demonstrate an atomic-scale method for engineering quantum states within the band gap of two-dimensional semiconductors.

item.title: [7] From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
item.description:
Last authors: David Valenzuela, Alfredo Raya

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory linking geometry to effective fields for Dirac/Weyl fermions, relevant to topological semimetals.

Tags: #theory #Diracfermions #Weylsemimetals #topological

Abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

item.title: [8] Hierarchical coupling in tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonics for a low-loss and tunable coupled-mode Hamiltonian
item.description:
Last authors: Hee Chul Park, Minkyung Jung

Authors: Taehee Kim, Sunghun Park, Byoung-moo Ann, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of vdW cavity magnonics in CrCl3, relevant to magnetic phenomena and vdW materials.

Tags: #vanderWaals #magnetism #magnonics #spectroscopy #experimental #CrCl3

Abstract: One of the greatest merits of cavity magnonics (CM) is the ability to explore rich coupled-mode physics, driven by the large \textit{in situ} flux tunability of magnonic resonances and magnon--photon coupling. Meanwhile, van der Waals (vdW) magnets offer an ultra-compact and highly integrated implementation of CM without complex fabrication processes. Nonetheless, the substantial magnon losses significantly hinder the combination of all these advantages. Here, we realize a hierarchical anti-crossing structure in a tripartite vdW CM with CrCl3 and realize an effective coupled-dual-mode Hamiltonian. We achieve an order-of-magnitude reduction in loss while maintaining a strong coupling condition. Additionally, we theoretically confirm the feasibility of simultaneous and \textit{in situ} tuning of both loss and coupling by varying the magnetic field direction and strength. Featuring a micrometer-scale thickness and a width of a few millimeters, our device is significantly smaller than those based on bulk crystals or crystal arrays. Our results establish vdW cavity magnonics as versatile platform for investigating intriguing phenomena predicted in coupled-mode systems.

item.title: [7] 1/N corrections to TJJ and TTT in QED3, QED3--GNY and scalar QED3
item.description:
Last authors: Zhijin Li, Ke Ren

Authors: Yongwei Guo, Zhijin Li, Ke Ren

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Formal theory paper with explicit connections to Dirac spin liquids, cuprates, and quantum critical points.

Tags: #theory #quantumcriticalpoint #cuprates #Diracsemimetal #superconductivity

Abstract: Three-dimensional Abelian gauge theories have broad applications in deconfined quantum criticality, Dirac spin liquids and cuprate superconductivity. Correlation functions of conserved currents $J$ and the stress tensor $T$ carry fundamental information about these theories. We compute the first subleading large-flavor corrections to the parity-even three-point functions $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--Gross--Neveu--Yukawa, and critical scalar QED$_3$. For $\langle TJJ\rangle$, we study both global flavor currents and the topological $U(1)$ current, which measures the magnetic flux of the dynamical gauge field. We evaluate the flat-space energy flux in directions where the leading free-field profile vanishes. At first subleading order the flux in these directions is determined by four-particle production, yielding analytic corrections to the conformal collider parameters. We reproduce the corrections independently from squashed-sphere free-energy derivatives. Together with known two-point normalizations, the collider parameters fix the coefficients of both independent tensor structures in each correlator. Our results are useful for studying conductivity and shear response near quantum critical points and for conformal bootstrap studies of conserved-current and stress-tensor correlators in strongly coupled gauge theories.

item.title: [7] 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
item.description:
Last authors: Ramani Duraiswami, Yichao Zhang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Advanced microscopy methodology (4D-STEM) for atomic structure, applied to relevant 2D materials (WSe2).

Tags: #methodology #microscopy #2Dmaterials #WSe2

Abstract: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty. We propose 4D-TEMPO, a differentiable physical renderer that fits the atoms, the microscope, and the detector directly to the recorded electron counts under a Poisson likelihood. The output is a list of atoms, each a Gaussian primitive with a 3D position, a thermal width, and a model-conditional error bar from the Fisher information. The Fisher information also conditions the solver, gives the dose (electrons per {\AA}$^2$) each parameter needs, and separates calibration from imaging. On a simulated WSe$_2$ bilayer, starting from the published reconstruction, fitted atoms cut in-plane error by a third (3.2 vs. 4.8 pm) and depth error by 40-61% against its 3D peaks. Depth comes from multiple scattering into the dark field, the faint counts outside the direct beam. The two layers, $10\times$ closer than the depth of field, separate; per-atom depth then follows the layer geometry. When the model is well specified, the bars are calibrated (69% of position coordinates within $1\sigma$). On experimental WSe$_2$, fitted atoms predict held-out patterns better than the three published codes we test. With free probe modes where atoms are incomplete, the same likelihood predicts best on all three held-out benchmarks, matches every WSe$_2$ baseline in 5 min against up to 20.5 h, and passes torchslice at its released setting 180$\times$ sooner on PrScO$_3$. Per-atom error bars, planned doses, and fast reconstruction point to low-dose, real-time 3D imaging of beam-sensitive and dynamic materials.

item.title: [7] Current-induced torque in a MoS2-based device operating at room temperature
item.description:
Last authors: Federico Caglieris, Ilaria Pallecchi

Authors: Antonio Bianco, Michele Ceccardi, Raimondo Cecchini, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Spin-orbit torque in 2D MoS2, discussing spin and orbital Hall effects with ab initio calculations.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #spintronics #spin-orbitcoupling #Halleffect #DFT

Abstract: Charge-to-spin and spin-to-charge conversion mechanisms in high spin-orbit materials are the new frontier of memory devices. They operate via spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching of a magnetic electrode, driven by an applied charge current. In this work, we propose a novel memory device based on the semiconducting two-dimensional centrosymmetric transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) MoS2, that operates as a SOT device in the writing process and as a non-local spin valve in the reading process. We demonstrate that stable voltage states at room temperature can be controlled by applied current and magnetic fields, owed to a locally tilted geometry and a differential voltage architecture. Ab initio calculations of orbital Hall effect (OHE) and spin Hall effect (SHE) indicate that the orbital Hall conductivity is constant and sizeable (750x(hbar/e) ohm-1 cm-1) throughout the conduction gap, while the spin Hall conductivity vanishes in the gap, thus pointing to the former as the most likely responsible for the generation of the SOT in the magnetic electrode, among intrinsic mechanisms. However, also extrinsic and interface spin-orbit mechanisms likely play a role. Our device concept may be competitive in terms of energy efficiency if an acceptable trade off with stability is obtained.

item.title: [9] Strain-induced splitting of the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition in 1T-TaS2
item.description:
Last authors: N. I. Fedotov, S. V. Zaitsev-Zotov

Authors: M. M. Tyumentsev, V. E. Minakova, N. I. Fedotov, S. V. Zaitsev-Zotov

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of strain effects on CDW transition and transport in 1T-TaS2, highly relevant to CDW interest.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #CDW #transport #strainengineering #transitionmetals

Abstract: The effects of uniaxial and biaxial tensile strain on the $\rho_{xx}$ and $\rho_{yy}$ components of the resistivity tensor and the commensurate --- nearly commensurate CDW (CCDW-NCCDW) transition temperature in 1T-TaS$_2$ are studied. At room temperature, uniaxial tensile strain increases the resistivity tensor components by a comparable magnitude both parallel and perpendicular to the strain axis. In the case of biaxial strain, up to 20~K decrease in the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperature is observed. In the case of uniaxial strain, a new phase with two different CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperatures is observed, the splitting exceeds 10 K. The occurrence of such a phase is associated with the transition of the CDW into the commensurate state along the tensile strain direction while maintaining nearly commensurability along the perpendicular one. The results allow to justify various models widely used in analysis of transport properties of 1T-TaS$_2$ in commensurate and nearly commensurate states.

item.title: [8] Temperature and spatial variation of topological defects density during the crystallization of vortex nanocrystals (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: A. B. Kolton, Y. Fasano

Authors: M. I. Dolz, A. B. Kolton, Y. Fasano

Published as: Phys. Rev. B DOI

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Simulation of topological defects in vortex nanocrystals in cuprate superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+delta.

Tags: #superconductivity #cuprates #vortexphysics #topologicaldefects #simulation

Abstract: Understanding the role of confinement while crystallizing nanocrystals is very relevant for predicting their structure and physical properties. With this aim we perform Langevin dynamics simulations of nanocrystals of the model system of few hundred vortices nucleated in micron-sized superconductors. We study the crystallization dynamics and the low-temperature structural properties of vortex nanocrystals nucleated in field-cooling conditions when changing vortex density or elasticity of the system and physical size of the samples. The low-temperature snapshots obtained in simulations present a healing effect at the edges that is in quantitative agreement with experimental data in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+{\delta} micron-sized samples. We show that the low-temperature radial distribution of topological defects is a stationary profile frozen at a temperature below the melting line tuned by intrinsic properties of the vortex structure and on the confinement effect. These findings on the dynamics and spatial profile of topological defects can be applied to describe the physical properties of confined soft condensed matter nanocrystals in general.

item.title: [7] Signatures of Gaussian superconducting fluctuations in nonlocal noise magnetometry (Phys. Rev. B)
item.description:
Last authors: Dror Orgad

Published as: Phys. Rev. B

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental probe of superconducting fluctuations in 2D/1D systems, relevant to unconventional superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #experimentalmethod #2Dmaterials #1Dmaterials

Abstract: We calculate the two-point magnetic noise spectrum arising from Gaussian superconducting fluctuations, a quantity directly measurable by spin qubit pairs such as nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond. The analysis utilizes the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory, reflecting the direct contribution of fluctuating Cooper pairs to the current correlations and consequent magnetic noise. We focus on two-dimensional systems and consider them both in equilibrium and under a uniform electric field. The signal is expected to be particularly pronounced in high-temperature superconductors, and we contrast our findings with the predicted signatures of a vortex liquid to offer an additional route to elucidate the nature of fluctuations in these systems. For completeness and comparison, we also present analogous results for one-dimensional wires.

item.title: [7] Bobkingite, a new coupled sawtooth chain platform
item.description:
Last authors: Antia S. Botana, Roser Valent\'i

Authors: P. Peter Stavropoulos, Aleksandar Razpopov, Harrison LaBollita, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Identifies a new quasi-one-dimensional material platform for sawtooth chain physics with computational methods.

Tags: #materialdiscovery #quasi-1D #magnetism #DFT

Abstract: We investigate the mineral bobkingite, $\mathrm{Cu}_5(\mathrm{OH})_8\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2$, as a potential realization of the sawtooth chain. Using ab initio methods, we estimate the magnetic exchange couplings and find that bobkingite hosts quasi-one-dimensional sawtooth chains, with residual three-dimensional interactions strongly suppressed by the crystal geometry. Examining the full exchange network, we find that the classical model exhibits an extensive manifold of nearly degenerate states with emergent two-dimensional character, which spin-wave theory shows to persist as Ising degrees of freedom. Unlike other sawtooth candidates, bobkingite has negligible vertical interchain coupling, preserving a one-dimensional degeneracy even in the presence of ordering, suggesting that any long-range order is weak. Thermal fluctuations stabilize a finite-temperature regime of multiplanar fluctuations rooted in the classical chain degeneracy, whose spin correlations resemble those of the quantum sawtooth chain, suggesting the persistence of quantum features in the full model. This makes bobkingite a compelling platform for exploring sawtooth chain physics.

item.title: [8] Colloquium: Semi-Dirac Fermions in Quantum Matter
item.description:
Last authors: Yinming Shao, Dmitri N. Basov

Authors: Bruno Uchoa, Mohamed M. Elsayed, Valeri N. Kotov, Yinming Shao, Dmitri N. Basov

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Colloquium reviewing semi-Dirac fermions in quantum materials, highly relevant to Dirac physics and Fermi surface.

Tags: #review #Diracfermions #Fermisurface #quantummaterials

Abstract: This article reviews the recent progress on the subject of semi-Dirac fermions, two dimensional quasiparticles that disperse quadratically, as Galilean invariant particles, or linearly, as massless relativistic particles, depending on their direction of motion. These quasiparticles exist at phase boundaries set by the continuous change in the connectivity of Fermi surfaces, known as Lifshitz transitions. The basic properties and the current experimental evidence of the existence of these quasiparticles in both synthetic lattices and quantum materials are presented. The many-body problem of semi-Dirac fermions is discussed from a theoretical perspective with an eye to physical observables of relevance to experiments.

item.title: [8] Landscape geometry of Majorana zero modes in inhomogeneous superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Kang Xu, C. P. Sun

Authors: Guo-Jian Qiao, Zhi-Lei Zhang, Kang Xu, C. P. Sun

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Develops a practical, profile-independent approach for characterizing Majorana zero modes in inhomogeneous superconductors.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #Majorana #topologicalsuperconductivity #superconductivity #theory #devicephysics

Abstract: Conventional methods for characterizing Majorana zero modes in inhomogeneous superconductors generally cannot be applied directly when the potential profile is unknown. To address this limitation, we propose a real-space approach based on a landscape for the zero-energy spatial dynamics. The landscape geometry determines the number of Majorana zero modes, and the conventional topological phase transition is recovered as a geometric transition of the landscape in the homogeneous limit. Without specifying detailed spatial profiles, the approach yields analytical bounds on Hamiltonian parameters and their spatial gradients that guarantee Majorana zero modes. item.title: [10] A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
item.description:
Last authors: Alexander A. Balandin, Md Shafayat Hossain

Authors: Chun-Tung Lien, Nidhish Thiruthukkal Puthenveettil, Alexander A. Balandin, Md Shafayat Hossain

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Perspective on topological CDW, directly mentioning kagome metals, Weyl, Berry curvature, superconductivity.

Tags: #review #CDW #kagome #topological #Weyl #Berry-curvature #superconductivity

Abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

item.title: [8] Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Tomoaki Kameda, Kazuhito Tsukagoshi

Authors: Katsunori Wakabayashi, Souren Adhikary, Tomoaki Kameda, Kazuhito Tsukagoshi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates ferroelectric valley transduction in bilayer WSe2, relevant to 2D materials and vdW heterostructures.

Tags: #2D-materials #valleytronics #ferroelectricity #transport #heterostructure

Abstract: Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $\Gamma$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$\Gamma$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches 41.7 meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only 0.2 % at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

item.title: [8] Symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state revealed by site-selective 13C NMR in -(BETS)2I3
item.description:
Last authors: Reizo Kato, Kazushi Kanoda

Authors: Takahiko Sekine, Kazuya Miyagawa, Koichi Hiraki, Reizo Kato, Kazushi Kanoda

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental NMR study of a symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state in a correlated topological material.

Tags: #Dirac #topological #correlated #NMR #organic-material

Abstract: We report evidence that the low-temperature insulating phase of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ preserves both inversion and time-reversal symmetries using site-selective $^{13}$C nuclear magnetic resonance. $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ undergoes a metal-insulator transition or sharp crossover at approximately 50 K and has been proposed as a candidate spin-orbit-coupling-induced Dirac insulator, yet the nature of its insulating ground state remains unresolved. The NMR spectra exhibit no additional splitting down to 2 K and remain fully described by one quartet and two doublets associated with the three types of molecular sites, A (=A$^{\prime}$), B and C sites, demonstrating the preservation of inversion symmetry. Furthermore, no anomalous line broadening or critical enhancement of the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate is observed, indicating the absence of magnetic ordering and time-reversal-symmetry breaking. Analysis of the Knight shifts yields site-specific spin susceptibilities satisfying $\chi_{\mathrm{C}} > \chi_{\mathrm{A}} > \chi_{\mathrm{B}}$, a characteristic feature of tilted Dirac-cone electronic states as observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$ under pressure. However, the faint field-induced ferrimagnetic-like spin excitations observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$, which are ascribed to the gapless tilted Dirac cones, are absent in $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$. These results demonstrate that the insulating ground state of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ is a symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state and provide microscopic constraints on proposed correlated topological phases in this molecular Dirac system.

item.title: [7] Spin disorder competing with positional symmetry breaking governs the metal-insulator behavior in oxide paramagnets
item.description:
Last authors: Xiuwen Zhang, Alex Zunger

Authors: Jia-Xin Xiong, Xiuwen Zhang, Alex Zunger

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT study of metal-insulator transition in transition-metal oxides relevant to correlated systems.

Tags: #theory #DFT #metal-insulatortransition #stronglycorrelated #oxides

Abstract: Numerous transition-metal oxides have low-temperature, long-range-ordered antiferromagnetic (AFM) states that are generally insulating, and high-temperature, disordered paramagnetic (PM) phases. The latter can be either insulating (predicted here for NaFeO3), or metallic (predicted here and previously observed in NaOsO3). Similar distinctions have been traditionally affected in strongly correlated models by the value used for Coulomb repulsion U. Here we show an alternative, strong-correlation-free (U=0) view suggesting that the distinction between insulating and metallic PM phases is governed by the competition between local magnetic moment disorder and the polymorphous distribution of off-center atomic displacements. Such parameter-free, energy-lowering symmetry breaking density functional calculations provide a framework for understanding metal-insulator behaviors across different quantum materials in terms of measurable local structural and magnetic parameters.

item.title: [7] Bogoliubov self-consistent GW and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
item.description:
Last authors: Johannes T\"olle, Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Loos

Authors: Mauricio Rodr{\'i}guez-Mayorga, Johannes T\"olle, Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Loos

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Methodological paper on GW/Green's function for attractive Hubbard/superconductors, relevant to correlated systems.

Tags: #methodology #theory #superconductivity #stronglycorrelated #Hubbardmodel #Green'sfunction

Abstract: Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov fully self-consistent $GW$ (Bog.~sc$GW$) and second-order Green's function (Bog.~scGF2) methods, implemented within a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework. Using two attractive Hubbard lattices ($4\times4$ and $2\times8$) as a model study and benchmarking against full configuration interaction (FCI), we find that, for these systems, Bog.~scGF2 provides a more accurate description than Bog.~sc$GW$. In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. These results suggest the importance of exchange contributions in such strongly correlated fermionic systems, even when exchange effects are included only at low order in perturbation theory.

item.title: [7] One Measurement, Many Fronts in Kitaev and Cluster Chains
item.description:
Last authors: Stephan Haas, Rishabh Jha

Authors: Nicholas Musat, Stephan Haas, Rishabh Jha

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Theoretical study of measurement dynamics and correlations in Kitaev topological chains, relevant to Majorana physics.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #theory #topological #Majorana #Kitaevmodel #quantummeasurement

Abstract: A projective measurement of one site in the ground state of a quantum chain disturbs the chain in two ways: learning the outcome shifts distant expectation values at once, through ground-state correlations, and the measurement erases the correlations between the measured site and the rest. Both changes travel outward. We solve this problem exactly for the Kitaev chain, the cluster chain in a transverse field, and the Kitaev chain with power-law couplings, and we find that far from the measured site every quadratic observable responds through a front. Where the front is and how fast it broadens depend only on the quasiparticle dispersion. How strong it is depends on two operators: how strongly the measured one creates the fastest quasiparticles and how strongly the observed one detects them; if either factor vanishes, the front is weaker and decays faster. One measurement therefore launches many fronts, one per observable, with a common position and width but different decay laws. In the Kitaev chain the density and the bond energy, the two terms of its nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian, respond to one density measurement with decay laws that trade places between the topological and the trivial phase; in the cluster chain, measuring a symmetry-odd spin instead of a symmetry-even one changes the critical decay law at a fixed Hamiltonian; and with power-law couplings the width law itself changes. All decay laws and profiles are obtained in closed form.

item.title: [7] Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
item.description:
Last authors: Guangyue Ji, Jie Wang

Authors: Xin Shen, Guangyue Ji, Jie Wang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of chiral spin liquids and fractional quantum Hall states, relevant for strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #theory #spinliquid #fractionalquantumHall #topologicalorder #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

item.title: [7] Delayed Formation of Landau Polaritons in Phase-Resolved THz Spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Wojciech Knap, Marcin Bialek

Authors: Noureddine Charrouj, Nischal Gajurel, Yurii Ivonyak, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of light-matter coupling in 2D electron gas systems.

Tags: #THzspectroscopy #polaritons #2Delectrongas

Abstract: Strong light-matter coupling gives rise to polaritons through coherent and periodic energy exchange between electromagnetic cavity fields and material excitations. While this interaction is typically inferred from spectral mode splitting, its dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, using phase-resolved terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we observe vacuum Rabi oscillations of Landau polaritons formed by coupling the cyclotron resonance in a GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron gas with Fabry-Perot cavity modes. By employing cross-polarized spectroscopy and magnetic-field differential, we resolve the temporal beating of the cyclotron resonance oscillations. Supported by a quantum electrodynamic model, we show that the vacuum Rabi oscillations start after a delay corresponding to one cavity round-trip time. This demonstrates that the strong coupling regime sets up only after the formation of the cavity mode field. Our results provide direct insight into the dynamics of hybrid light-matter states in the THz regime.
